title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
知者不惑仁者不憂勇者不懼
詩曰在彼無惡在此無射庶幾夙夜以永
終譽君子未有不如此而蚤有譽於天
下者也
其爲氣也至大至剛以直養而無害則塞
于天地之間
易
===
象曰天地交泰后以財成天地之道輔相
天地之宜以左右民
王假有廟致孝享也
引而伸之觸類而長之天下之能事畢矣
易之爲書也不可遠爲道也屢遷變動不
居周流六虛上下无常剛柔相易不可
爲典要唯變所適
書
水火金木土穀惟修正德利用厚生惟和
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

知者不惑，仁者不憂，勇者不懼。

詩曰：「在彼無惡，在此無射，庶幾夙夜，以永終譽。」君子未有不如此而蚤有譽於天下者也。

其爲氣也，至大至剛，以直養而無害，則塞于天地之間。

易

象曰：「天地交，泰。后以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。」

王假有廟，致孝享也。

引而伸之，觸類而長之，天下之能事畢矣。

易之爲書也，不可遠；爲道也，屢遷。變動不居，周流六虛，上下无常，剛柔相易，不可爲典要，唯變所適。

書

水、火、金、木、土、穀，惟修；正德、利用、厚生，惟和。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The wise are not perplexed; the benevolent are not anxious; the courageous are not afraid.

The Book of Odes says: “There, he is not hated; here, he causes no weariness. May he strive morning and night, to preserve his good name forever.” No gentleman has ever won an early reputation throughout the world without acting in this way.

As a vital force, it is supremely great and supremely firm. If nourished with uprightness and left unharmed, it fills the space between Heaven and Earth.

Book of Changes

The Commentary on the Images says: “Heaven and Earth interact: Peace. The sovereign accordingly regulates and brings to completion the Way of Heaven and Earth, assists what is fitting in Heaven and Earth, and thereby supports and guides the people.”

“The king comes to the ancestral temple”: this means offering sacrifice with the utmost filial devotion.

By drawing out and extending these principles, and developing them through analogous cases, all that can be accomplished in the world is encompassed.

The Changes is a book from which one must not remain distant; as a Way, it shifts repeatedly. It changes and moves without rest, circulating through the six vacant positions. Its ascent and descent follow no constant pattern; the firm and the yielding exchange places. It cannot be taken as a fixed rule: it follows wherever change leads.

Book of Documents

Water, fire, metal, wood, earth, and grain must be properly managed; the rectification of virtue, the provision of useful resources, and the enrichment of the people’s livelihood must be brought into harmony.

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
監于先王成憲其永無愆
凡厥庶民無有淫朋人無有比德惟皇作
極
乃命三后恤功于民伯夷降典折民惟刑
禹平水土主名山川稷降播種農殖嘉
穀三后成功惟殷于民
詩
有杕之杜生于道左彼君子兮噬肯適我
中心好之曷飲食之
===
春日遲遲卉木萋萋倉庚喈喈采蘩祁祁
執訊獲醜薄言還歸赫赫南仲玁狁于
夷
賦政于外四方爰發
喤喤厥聲肅雝和鳴先祖是聽我客戾止
永觀厥成
春秋
春鄭人來輸平〔隱公六年〕三月鄭伯使宛來
歸祊庚寅我入祊〔隱公八年〕鄭伯以璧
punctuated:
監于先王成憲，其永無愆。
凡厥庶民，無有淫朋，人無有比德，惟皇作極。
乃命三后恤功于民：伯夷降典，折民惟刑；禹平水土，主名山川；稷降播種，農殖嘉穀。三后成功，惟殷于民。

詩
有杕之杜，生于道左。彼君子兮，噬肯適我？中心好之，曷飲食之？
春日遲遲，卉木萋萋。倉庚喈喈，采蘩祁祁。執訊獲醜，薄言還歸。赫赫南仲，玁狁于夷。
賦政于外，四方爰發。
喤喤厥聲，肅雝和鳴，先祖是聽。我客戾止，永觀厥成。

春秋
春，鄭人來輸平。〔隱公六年〕三月，鄭伯使宛來歸祊。庚寅，我入祊。〔隱公八年〕鄭伯以璧
translation_en:
Look to the established statutes of the former kings, and you will forever be without error.
Among all the common people, let there be no improper cliques, and let no one practice partisan conduct. Let the sovereign alone establish the supreme standard.
He then charged the three lords with attending to works for the people. Bo Yi promulgated the statutes, guiding the people by proper standards; Yu brought order to the waters and the land and presided over the renowned mountains and rivers; Ji taught sowing and planting, cultivating fine grain. The three lords accomplished their work, bringing abundance to the people.

Book of Odes (Shi)
A solitary wild pear tree grows to the left of the road. Would that gentleman be willing to come to me? In my heart I cherish him; why should I not give him food and drink?
The spring days lengthen; plants and trees grow luxuriantly. Orioles sing in harmony; those gathering white southernwood come in throngs. We seized prisoners for questioning and captured the enemy; then we returned home. Glorious was Nan Zhong: the Xianyun were subdued.
He issued orders beyond the court, and the four quarters sprang into action.
Resonant are their sounds, solemn and harmonious as they sound together; the ancestors listen. Our guest has arrived, long to behold their accomplishment.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
In spring, men of Zheng came to offer peace. 〔Sixth year of Duke Yin〕 In the third month, the Earl of Zheng sent Wan to return Beng to us. On the gengyin day, we entered Beng. 〔Eighth year of Duke Yin〕 The Earl of Zheng, with a jade disk…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
假許田〔桓公元年〕
冬楚人伐黃〔僖公十有一年〕
夏六月乙卯晉荀林父帥師及楚子戰于
邲晉師敗績〔宣公十有二年〕晉欒書帥師救
鄭〔成公六年〕
八月晉荀吳帥師滅陸渾之戎〔昭公十有七年〕
禮記
天子以德爲車以樂爲御諸侯以禮相與
大夫以法相序士以信相考百姓以睦
===
相守天下之肥也
天尊地卑君臣定矣卑高以陳貴賤位矣
動靜有常大小殊矣方以類聚物以羣
分則性命不同矣在天成象在地成形
如此則禮者天地之别也地氣上齊天
氣下降陰陽相摩天地相蕩鼓之以雷
霆奮之以風雨動之以四時煖之以日
月而百化興焉如此則樂者天地之和
也
punctuated:
假許田〔桓公元年〕。
冬，楚人伐黃〔僖公十有一年〕。
夏六月乙卯，晉荀林父帥師及楚子戰于邲，晉師敗績〔宣公十有二年〕。晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕。
八月，晉荀吳帥師滅陸渾之戎〔昭公十有七年〕。

禮記
天子以德爲車，以樂爲御；諸侯以禮相與，大夫以法相序，士以信相考，百姓以睦相守，天下之肥也。
天尊地卑，君臣定矣；卑高以陳，貴賤位矣；動靜有常，大小殊矣；方以類聚，物以羣分，則性命不同矣。在天成象，在地成形，如此則禮者天地之别也。地氣上齊，天氣下降，陰陽相摩，天地相蕩，鼓之以雷霆，奮之以風雨，動之以四時，煖之以日月，而百化興焉。如此則樂者天地之和也。
translation_en:
… borrowed the fields of Xu. 〔First year of Duke Huan.〕
In winter, the men of Chu attacked Huang. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xi.〕
In summer, on the yimao day of the sixth month, Xun Linfu of Jin led an army into battle against the Viscount of Chu at Bi. The Jin army suffered a crushing defeat. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xuan.〕 Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. 〔Sixth year of Duke Cheng.〕
In the eighth month, Xun Wu of Jin led an army and destroyed the Rong of Luhun. 〔Seventeenth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Record of Rites (Liji)
The Son of Heaven takes virtue as his carriage and music as his charioteer. The feudal lords associate with one another through ritual; the great officers order their ranks according to established rules; the gentlemen assess one another by their trustworthiness; and the common people protect one another in harmony. This is the flourishing of all under Heaven.
Heaven is exalted and Earth is lowly: thus the relations of ruler and minister are established. Low and high are arrayed: thus noble and humble have their places. Movement and stillness have their constant patterns: thus great and small are distinguished. Things gather according to their kinds and divide into groups: thus their natures and allotted destinies differ. In Heaven, images take shape; on Earth, forms take shape. Thus ritual embodies the distinctions of Heaven and Earth. Earth's vital breath rises, and Heaven's vital breath descends. Yin and yang interact, and Heaven and Earth stir one another. They arouse things with thunder, quicken them with wind and rain, set them in motion through the four seasons, and warm them with the sun and moon; all the myriad transformations thereby arise. Thus music embodies the harmony of Heaven and Earth.

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
尊仁安義可謂用勞矣
垂之如隊禮也叩之其聲清越以長其終
詘然樂也
第貳場
論
君子尊德性而道問學
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢舉賢良文學詔〔始元六年〕
擬唐以孫伏伽爲治書侍御史誥〔武德元年〕
擬宋以趙普爲司徒兼侍中謝表〔太平興 國六年〕
===
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
欺隱田糧
御賜衣物
宿衛人兵仗
修理倉庫
第叄場
punctuated:
尊仁安義，可謂用勞矣。
垂之如隊，禮也；叩之，其聲清越以長，其終詘然，樂也。

第貳場
論：君子尊德性而道問學。
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢舉賢良文學詔〔始元六年〕。
擬唐以孫伏伽爲治書侍御史誥〔武德元年〕。
擬宋以趙普爲司徒兼侍中謝表〔太平興 國六年〕。

判語〔五條〕
官吏給由。
欺隱田糧。
御賜衣物。
宿衛人兵仗。
修理倉庫。

第叄場
translation_en:
To honor benevolence and abide in righteousness may be called exerting oneself.
Hanging down as though falling, it exemplifies ritual propriety; when struck, its sound is clear, resonant, and sustained, ending abruptly: this exemplifies music.

Second Session
Discourse: “The gentleman honors his moral nature and pursues inquiry and learning.”
Imperial edicts, appointment proclamations, and memorials 〔One item from this category [?].〕
Compose a simulated Han edict calling for the recommendation of worthy and upright men and men of literary learning. 〔Sixth year of Shiyuan.〕
Compose a simulated Tang proclamation appointing Sun Fuga as Censor for Document Review (zhishu shiyushi). 〔First year of Wude.〕
Compose a simulated Song memorial of thanks for the appointment of Zhao Pu as Minister of Education and concurrently Palace Attendant. 〔Sixth year of Taiping Xingguo.〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items.〕
Issuing certificates of service to officials and clerks.
Fraudulent concealment of farmland and grain-tax obligations.
Imperially bestowed clothing and other articles.
Weapons of palace guards.
Repairing granaries and storehouses.

Third Session

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
策〔五道〕
問自古創業之君必定一代法制為子孫
世守自今觀之國之急務最宜裁酌精
審俾永久不敝者尤在于財與兵而已
蓋民以財為心以兵為衛國家安危所
係焉者孔子論政所以先乎此也洪惟
我
太祖高皇帝戡定禍亂統一華夏
太宗文皇帝再清海宇
===
英謨睿訓所以垂示乎
聖子神孫者至精且備矣若
皇明政要一書紀我
祖宗嘉言善行者四十條中有節財用賑荒歉
脩武備固封守四事其詳可得聞與
國家仰承
皇祖之訓有
國以來家給人足四方無虞久矣今
聖天子脩復中興之治懷保民無窮之心每憂
punctuated:
策〔五道〕

問：自古創業之君，必定一代法制，為子孫世守。自今觀之，國之急務，最宜裁酌精審，俾永久不敝者，尤在于財與兵而已。蓋民以財為心，以兵為衛，國家安危所係焉者，孔子論政所以先乎此也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝戡定禍亂，統一華夏，太宗文皇帝再清海宇，英謨睿訓，所以垂示乎聖子神孫者，至精且備矣。若《皇明政要》一書，紀我祖宗嘉言善行者四十條，中有節財用、賑荒歉、脩武備、固封守四事，其詳可得聞與？國家仰承皇祖之訓，有國以來，家給人足，四方無虞久矣。今聖天子脩復中興之治，懷保民無窮之心，每憂
translation_en:
Policy questions 〔five questions〕

Question: Since antiquity, rulers who founded dynasties have invariably established laws and institutions for their dynasty, to be maintained by their descendants generation after generation. Viewed from the present, among the urgent affairs of state, those that particularly require the most careful deliberation and scrutiny, so that they may endure forever without falling into disrepair, are finance and military affairs. For the people regard wealth as their central concern and troops as their protection; the security or peril of the state depends upon these. This is why Confucius gave them priority in discussing government. We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao quelled calamity and disorder and unified the Chinese realm, and Emperor Taizong Wen once again pacified all within the seas. The illustrious plans and sagacious instructions they bequeathed to their sage sons and divine grandsons were supremely refined and comprehensive. The book Essentials of Government of the August Ming (Huang Ming Zhengyao), for example, records the admirable words and good deeds of our imperial ancestors in forty articles. Among them are four matters: economizing on expenditure, providing relief for famine and poor harvests, strengthening military preparedness, and securing territorial defenses. May we hear their particulars?

The state has reverently upheld the instructions of the imperial ancestors. Since the founding of the dynasty, households have enjoyed sufficiency and individuals plenty, and the four quarters have long been free from danger. Now our sagely Son of Heaven restores the governance of dynastic resurgence and cherishes an enduring desire to protect the people, constantly worrying …

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
及此然禁奢之
詔屢下而
國賦未充救荒之策屢講而凶歲迭見部伍
多缺邊陲數警誠不可無備也
祖宗之法有可申明丁
今日請敬陳之〔勿略〕
問禮者所以辨上下定民志也國非禮不
治家非禮不正學非禮不立周禮一書
法制最備論者曰周公致太平之書又
===
曰文王治岐之書又曰成周理財之書
或又曰漢儒附會之書何所見之不同
與今者其故又大有可議者且周禮周
官一代之制也周官首三公次三孤次
六卿次百司周禮有六卿而無公孤周
官紀天子諸侯巡狩朝覲之期周禮無
其文茲非細事可略也何相背若是與
周禮缺冬官或者以考工記補之考工
之說可盡冬官之意否與或者又為諸
punctuated:
及此。然禁奢之詔屢下，而國賦未充；救荒之策屢講，而凶歲迭見，部伍多缺，邊陲數警，誠不可無備也。祖宗之法有可申明丁今日，請敬陳之。〔勿略〕
問：禮者，所以辨上下、定民志也。國非禮不治，家非禮不正，學非禮不立。《周禮》一書，法制最備。論者曰：「周公致太平之書。」又曰：「文王治岐之書。」又曰：「成周理財之書。」或又曰：「漢儒附會之書。」何所見之不同與？今者，其故又大有可議者。且《周禮》《周官》，一代之制也。《周官》首三公，次三孤，次六卿，次百司；《周禮》有六卿而無公孤。《周官》紀天子諸侯巡狩朝覲之期，《周禮》無其文。茲非細事可略也，何相背若是與？《周禮》缺冬官，或者以《考工記》補之。《考工》之說，可盡冬官之意否與？或者又為諸
translation_en:
…extends to these matters. Yet edicts prohibiting extravagance have repeatedly been issued, while the state's tax revenues remain insufficient; measures for famine relief have repeatedly been discussed, while years of dearth recur. Military units are seriously understrength, and alarms repeatedly arise along the frontiers. Truly, preparations cannot be neglected. Please respectfully set forth those laws of the imperial ancestors that might be reaffirmed today [?]. 〔Do not omit details.〕
Question: Ritual serves to distinguish superior from inferior and to give the people's aspirations a settled direction. Without ritual, the state cannot be governed, the household cannot be set right, and learning cannot be established. The Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) is a book in which laws and institutions are most fully provided. Commentators call it “the book through which the Duke of Zhou brought about great peace.” Others call it “the book through which King Wen governed Qi,” or “the book on managing the finances of the Zhou dynasty,” while still others call it “a book pieced together by Han Confucian scholars through forced associations.” Why do their views differ so greatly? Now, there is also much to discuss concerning the reasons for this. Both the Rites of Zhou and the “Offices of Zhou” (Zhouguan) present the institutions of a single dynasty. The “Offices of Zhou” places the Three Dukes first, followed by the Three Solitaries, then the Six Ministers, and then the many offices. The Rites of Zhou has the Six Ministers but no Dukes or Solitaries. The “Offices of Zhou” records the prescribed times for the Son of Heaven's inspection tours and the feudal lords' court audiences, whereas the Rites of Zhou contains no such passages. These are not minor matters that can be omitted. Why do the two contradict each other so markedly? The Rites of Zhou lacks the section on the Offices of Winter; some have supplied the Record of Artificers (Kaogong ji) to fill the gap. Can the explanations in the Record of Artificers fully convey the intended scope of the Offices of Winter? Others have further made [?]…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
之果得作者之意與後世有慕其書而
行之者往往未獲其效果書之罪邪抑
行之者未善也我
國家制度準周官而作而其間有不同者此
又何故也今百六十年承平既久而治
化浹洽正制禮作樂明光德業之時不
知周禮為書尚有可補我
國家之治者乎而古禮果可復于今否乎諸
士請著于篇以覘他日為國之術
===
問人心與天地一本善反之則天地之性
存焉詩之秉彝物則書之精一執中古
今言性言學者之權輿也後世大儒有
以中興豪傑自謂者其論性也則以孟
子之言未備無以服告子之心其論學
也則以朱子道問學爲多而於尊德性
若在所憾者今觀七篇之中言性善者
不一而足朱子則集諸儒之大成者乃
以為未備而偏許焉者何也考之於書
punctuated:
之，果得作者之意與？後世有慕其書而行之者，往往未獲其效，果書之罪邪？抑行之者未善也？我國家制度準《周官》而作，而其間有不同者，此又何故也？今百六十年，承平既久，而治化浹洽，正制禮作樂、明光德業之時。不知《周禮》為書，尚有可補我國家之治者乎？而古禮果可復于今否乎？諸士請著于篇，以覘他日為國之術。

問：人心與天地一本，善反之，則天地之性存焉。《詩》之秉彝物則，《書》之精一執中，古今言性言學者之權輿也。後世大儒有以中興豪傑自謂者，其論性也，則以孟子之言未備，無以服告子之心；其論學也，則以朱子道問學爲多，而於尊德性若在所憾者。今觀七篇之中，言性善者不一而足；朱子則集諸儒之大成者，乃以為未備而偏許焉者，何也？考之於《書》，
translation_en:
…did this truly capture the author's intention? In later ages, those who admired this book and put it into practice often failed to obtain the intended results. Was this really the book's fault, or did those implementing it fail to do so properly? Our dynasty's institutions were established on the model of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), yet there are differences between them. Why is this? Now, after 160 years, peace has long prevailed, and the transforming influence of good government has spread everywhere. This is precisely the time to establish rites and music and bring our virtuous achievements to full brilliance. Does the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) still contain anything that could supplement our dynasty's governance? Can ancient rites indeed be restored today? Let you candidates set out your views in writing, so that we may discern your methods for governing the state in the future.

Question: The human mind and Heaven and Earth share a single root. If one returns to it properly, the nature of Heaven and Earth is preserved within oneself. The Odes speaks of holding fast to constant moral principles and of the norms inherent in things; the Documents speaks of refinement and singleness of purpose and of holding fast to the Mean. These are the starting points for discussions of human nature and learning, ancient and modern. Among the great Confucian scholars of later ages was one who styled himself a heroic figure in the revival of the Way. In discussing human nature, he held that Mengzi's account was incomplete and could not convince Gaozi. In discussing learning, he held that Master Zhu devoted greater attention to inquiry and study, while seemingly leaving something to be desired in honoring the moral nature. Yet when we examine the seven books of the Mengzi, we find numerous statements that human nature is good; and Master Zhu brought the work of the Confucian scholars together into a grand synthesis. Why, then, judge the former incomplete and the latter one-sided? Examining this in the Documents…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
若臯陶曰九德箕子曰三德豈剛柔善
惡固亦可以言性而未備云者是歟一
道與二程之於二陸其兄弟師友之間
所以共力斯道宜無不同者一則以記
誦為玩物喪志一則欲將聖人言語玩
味入心一則宗程氏之學不移於俗一
則聽伊川之語而詆其非豈其所入之
途自得之趣各有不同然乎與朱子之
學同歸者何與茲欲究性善之原不知
所以為入門實地者安在也請言之以
觀一以貫之之學
===
問詩曰高山仰止景行行止諸君子生長
伊洛之地景仰有在試舉一時師友淵
源之懿商之夫程氏上接孟氏所謂千
載不傳之緒者可得聞與嗣是而傳其
學者甚衆其不謬於聖人者鮮矣望重
道南者不免於晚出之議學稱美才者
莫逃於禪學之譏過化便所存者神□
punctuated:
若臯陶曰九德，箕子曰三德，豈剛柔善惡固亦可以言性，而未備云者是歟？一道與？二程之於二陸，其兄弟師友之間，所以共力斯道，宜無不同者。一則以記誦為玩物喪志，一則欲將聖人言語玩味入心；一則宗程氏之學，不移於俗，一則聽伊川之語而詆其非。豈其所入之途、自得之趣，各有不同然乎？與朱子之學同歸者何與？茲欲究性善之原，不知所以為入門實地者安在也？請言之，以觀一以貫之之學。

問：詩曰：「高山仰止，景行行止。」諸君子生長伊洛之地，景仰有在，試舉一時師友淵源之懿商之。夫程氏上接孟氏，所謂千載不傳之緒者，可得聞與？嗣是而傳其學者甚衆，其不謬於聖人者鮮矣。望重道南者，不免於晚出之議；學稱美才者，莫逃於禪學之譏。過化便所存者神□
translation_en:
…For example, Gao Yao spoke of nine virtues, and Jizi spoke of three virtues. Can firmness and yielding, goodness and evil, indeed all be used to speak of human nature? Is this what is meant by saying that the account was incomplete? Is it one Way [?]? As for the two Cheng brothers and the two Lu brothers, their efforts to advance this Way, within their relationships as brothers, teachers, and friends, ought surely to have been in agreement. Yet one regarded memorization and recitation as toying with things and losing one’s resolve, while another wished to ponder the sages’ words until they entered the heart. One adhered to the learning of the Cheng masters without being swayed by prevailing customs, while another heard Yichuan’s words and denounced them as wrong. Could their paths of entry and the tenor of their personal understanding really have differed in each case? Which converged with Master Zhu’s learning? Now, wishing to investigate the source of the goodness of human nature, I ask: where is the firm ground on which to begin? Please explain, so that we may examine the learning in which a single principle runs through everything.

Question: The Book of Odes says, “We look up to the lofty mountain; we travel along the great road.” You gentlemen were born and raised in the Yi and Luo region, and have worthy objects of admiration. Let us consider the excellence of the intellectual lineages linking the teachers and friends of that time. The Cheng masters reached back to continue the tradition of Master Meng—the thread said to have gone untransmitted for a thousand years. May we hear an account of this? Thereafter, very many transmitted their learning, but few avoided departing from the sages. The man renowned for carrying the Way south did not escape criticism concerning his later years [?]; the man praised as a fine talent in learning could not escape the charge of Chan Buddhist learning. “Where he passes, transformation occurs” is then “where he abides, his influence is spiritual” [illegible character; wording doubtful]…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
神便所過者化其言視性性為能存神
物物為能過化者同與異與由誠而至
明由明而至誠其旨與誠則明矣明則
誠矣者同與異與易未易通也而終乃
謂之通易者何與春秋未易傳也而有
獨屬之為傳者何與聽講論語者何為
得一貫之旨能道中庸者何由得不逆
於心四賢之詠為洛中一時之壯其言
辭何者為近最愛之稱為高弟一時之
===
評其氣象何者為優以高識入者何以
有俊逸之稱以篤行入者何以有終守
之論而請益之方其於二者孰為切與
有尊嚴自處者何以自謂有所不及有
和易可親者何以衆皆悅從而成就之
益其於二者孰居多與至稱不雜者三
人不失其正者一人其亦有所試與凡
此皆道學源流之所繫而當時之教必
有最親切處可指言與噫典刑不遠遺
punctuated: 神便所過者化。其言視性性為能存神、物物為能過化者，同與異與？由誠而至明，由明而至誠，其旨與誠則明矣、明則誠矣者，同與異與？易未易通也，而終乃謂之通易者，何與？春秋未易傳也，而有獨屬之為傳者，何與？聽講論語者，何為得一貫之旨？能道中庸者，何由得不逆於心？四賢之詠，為洛中一時之壯，其言辭何者為近？最愛之稱，為高弟一時之評，其氣象何者為優？以高識入者，何以有俊逸之稱？以篤行入者，何以有終守之論？而請益之方，其於二者孰為切與？有尊嚴自處者，何以自謂有所不及？有和易可親者，何以衆皆悅從？而成就之益，其於二者孰居多與？至稱不雜者三人，不失其正者一人，其亦有所試與？凡此皆道學源流之所繫，而當時之教，必有最親切處，可指言與？噫！典刑不遠，遺
translation_en:
…spiritual efficacy is precisely the transforming influence exerted wherever one passes. Does this statement agree with or differ from the assertion that fully realizing one’s nature enables one to preserve spiritual efficacy, and treating things as things enables one to exert transforming influence wherever one passes [?]? To proceed from sincerity to understanding, and from understanding to sincerity: is the purport of this the same as, or different from, saying that sincerity brings understanding and understanding brings sincerity? The Book of Changes is not easy to comprehend; why, then, was someone ultimately said to comprehend it? The Spring and Autumn Annals is not easy to transmit; why, then, was someone entrusted exclusively with transmitting it? How did one who listened to lectures on the Analects grasp the purport of the single thread running through it? How did one who could expound the Doctrine of the Mean attain an understanding that met with no resistance in his heart?

The verses on the four worthies were a splendid expression of their time in the Luo region: whose words came closest to the Way? The designation “most beloved” was an appraisal of an outstanding disciple at that time: whose bearing was superior? Why was one who entered the school through lofty discernment praised as exceptionally gifted and untrammeled? Why was one who entered through steadfast practice said to hold firm to the end? Of these two approaches, which is more pertinent to seeking further instruction? Why did one who maintained a dignified and solemn bearing say himself that there were respects in which he fell short? Why did everyone gladly follow one who was gentle, easygoing, and approachable? Which of these two offered greater benefit in bringing learners to maturity? As for the three men described as free from admixture and the one described as not departing from rectitude, had they also been put to the test?

All these matters bear upon the origins and transmission of the Learning of the Way. Surely the teaching of that time had points of particular directness and relevance: can you identify and explain them? Ah! Those exemplars are not far removed, and their lingering…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
風猶存諸君子必有心存得師而相契
予者執事者願有聞也
問自箕子陳洪範以人之五事配天之五
行所感休咎各以類應其論精矣然漢
諸子五行傳皆原於春秋洪範以陰陽
徵應爲言互有異同其間旁引曲證似
有發明者而乃有深辨其非者何與又
謂以孔子作春秋言災異而不言事應
斷之若然則休咎之理將難指陳而洪
===
範五事之論不免膠固不通不足以語
造化之妙矣五代史著其災異削其徵
應或謂其妖妄之學欺天欺人衆說紛
紛何所取乎則彼休咎之徵何以別於
箕疇而感應之理不幾於息耶不知與
天人相與流通無間果何所得與恭惟
皇上聰明憲天側身修德其興除利弊率作事
功而惓惓於
宵旰之憂圖宜諸福之物可致之祥無不畢
punctuated:
風猶存。諸君子必有心存得師而相契予者，執事者願有聞也。
問：自箕子陳《洪範》，以人之五事配天之五行，所感休咎，各以類應，其論精矣。然漢諸子《五行傳》皆原於《春秋》《洪範》，以陰陽徵應爲言，互有異同。其間旁引曲證，似有發明者，而乃有深辨其非者，何與？又謂以孔子作《春秋》，言災異而不言事應斷之。若然，則休咎之理將難指陳，而《洪範》五事之論不免膠固不通，不足以語造化之妙矣。《五代史》著其災異，削其徵應，或謂其妖妄之學欺天欺人。衆說紛紛，何所取乎？則彼休咎之徵，何以別於箕疇，而感應之理不幾於息耶？不知與天人相與流通無間，果何所得與？恭惟皇上聰明憲天，側身修德，其興除利弊，率作事功，而惓惓於宵旰之憂圖，宜諸福之物、可致之祥，無不畢
translation_en:
…their influence still survives. Among you gentlemen there must surely be those whose resolve to find a teacher accords with my own. We who conduct this examination would welcome hearing from you.
Question: When Jizi expounded the Great Plan (Hongfan), he correlated the five human activities with Heaven’s Five Phases. The favorable and unfavorable effects elicited by them responded each according to its kind: a subtle account indeed. Yet the Han scholars’ Traditions of the Five Phases all derived from the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Great Plan, discussing manifestations and responses in terms of yin and yang, with both agreements and differences among their accounts. Some drew extensively on other sources and adduced elaborate corroboration, seemingly illuminating the subject; yet others argued searchingly that they were wrong. Why was this? It has also been said that the matter should be decided by the example of Confucius, who, in composing the Spring and Autumn Annals, recorded disasters and anomalies without specifying the human events to which they corresponded. If so, the principles underlying favorable and unfavorable effects would be difficult to explain concretely, while the Great Plan’s account of the five activities would inevitably become rigid and unworkable, inadequate to discuss the subtleties of creation and transformation.
The History of the Five Dynasties recorded disasters and anomalies but omitted their corresponding manifestations and responses. Some have called this bizarre and delusive learning a deception of Heaven and of humankind. Amid these conflicting opinions, which should we adopt? How, then, do those signs of favorable and unfavorable outcomes differ from the categories set out by Jizi? Would not the principle of stimulus and response come close to being extinguished? It is unclear what understanding has actually been gained concerning the uninterrupted mutual communication between Heaven and humankind [?].
We reverently consider how His Majesty, in his wisdom, takes Heaven as his model and humbly cultivates his virtue. He promotes benefits and removes abuses, leading the undertaking of meritorious works, and remains devoted to anxious deliberation from before dawn until late at night. Surely every blessing and every auspicious sign that can be brought about should, without exception, fully…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
至矣夫何邇年以來災異屢見其召致
之由消弭之方關於人事者二三子試
極言之毋
當宁之所欲聞也
punctuated: 至矣。夫何邇年以來，災異屢見？其召致之由、消弭之方，關於人事者，二三子試極言之。毋當宁之所欲聞也。
translation_en: …have all arrived. Why, then, have calamities and anomalies repeatedly appeared in recent years? You gentlemen, set forth fully the causes that have brought them about and the means of dispelling them, insofar as these concern human affairs. This is what the sovereign wishes to hear [?: the preceding character 毋, “do not,” makes the closing sentence unclear].

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
知者不惑仁者不憂勇者不懼
吳三樂
同考試官教諭劉　批〔此學之序作者多狃於中〕
〔庸達德之說殊失本旨求其體認親切意味雋永僅見此篇〕
同考試官教諭辛　批〔模寫不惑不憂不懼自是典則〕
考試官學正王　批〔意明語潔〕
考試官教授許　批〔平實〕
===
聖人言進學之序欲人知所求也夫知仁勇學
者所當求至焉者也否則惑與憂懼不免矣可
不自勉也哉夫子示人之意如此蓋曰夫人不
可闕焉者求道之功也不可紊焉者進學之序
也是故學以知爲先人之不能無所疑者必
其知之未至也夫惟知焉理之散於萬而原於
一者先明諸心矣虛靈之體寂而涵也明覺之
用感而通也凡事理之幾而聞見之知非
所溺矣夫何惑知以仁守爲貴人之不能無所
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

知者不惑，仁者不憂，勇者不懼。

吳三樂

同考試官教諭劉批〔此學之序，作者多狃於中〕〔庸達德之說，殊失本旨。求其體認親切，意味雋永，僅見此篇。〕

同考試官教諭辛批〔模寫不惑、不憂、不懼，自是典則。〕

考試官學正王批〔意明語潔。〕

考試官教授許批〔平實。〕

聖人言進學之序，欲人知所求也。夫知仁勇，學者所當求至焉者也。否則惑與憂懼不免矣，可不自勉也哉？夫子示人之意如此。蓋曰：夫人不可闕焉者，求道之功也；不可紊焉者，進學之序也。是故學以知爲先。人之不能無所疑者，必其知之未至也。夫惟知焉，理之散於萬而原於一者，先明諸心矣。虛靈之體，寂而涵也；明覺之用，感而通也。凡事理之幾，而聞見之知非所溺矣。夫何惑？知以仁守爲貴。人之不能無所
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“The wise are not perplexed; the benevolent are not anxious; the courageous are not afraid.”

Wu Sanle

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔This concerns the sequence of learning. Most writers are constrained by the Doctrine of the〕〔Mean’s account of the universally applicable virtues, entirely missing the original purport. For intimate understanding and enduring depth of meaning, this essay alone stands out.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Xin, Instructor: 〔Its portrayal of being unperplexed, free from anxiety, and unafraid is exemplary indeed.〕

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: 〔Clear ideas and concise language.〕

Comment by Examiner Xu, Professor: 〔Plain and solid.〕

The sage speaks of the sequence of advancement in learning so that people may know what to seek. Wisdom, benevolence, and courage are what learners should seek to attain fully. Otherwise, perplexity, anxiety, and fear are unavoidable. How could one fail to exert oneself? Such is the Master’s intention in instructing others. His meaning is this: what a person must not neglect is the effort to seek the Way; what must not be disordered is the sequence of advancement in learning. Thus learning begins with wisdom. If a person cannot be free of doubt, it must be because his wisdom has not reached its fullness. Only with wisdom does principle—which is dispersed among the myriad things yet originates in unity—first become clear within the mind. The mind’s vacuous and numinous substance is still and all-embracing; its luminous awareness responds to stimuli and penetrates them. As for the subtle workings of principle in affairs, one is not submerged in knowledge acquired through hearing and seeing [?]. What perplexity, then, could there be? title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
憂者必其仁之未至也夫惟仁焉理之純乎天
而不雜以人者復還於我矣順理則裕無愆於
志也隨寓而安無動於中也理以勝天下之私
而物欲之累非所患矣夫何憂至若仁知合一
而勇以強之斯學之全也然勇有未至則懼心
生矣夫惟勇焉浩然之氣善養其初天德之剛
克全於我則見義必為當大任不動其心也自
反而縮遇事變不喪其守也中有所主而外無
所慮矣何懼之有邪是知不惑則知至而道以
明不憂則仁至而道以行不懼則勇之至而道
===
亦無不強矣學者可不驗吾學之所至而求以
造其極哉抑是道也即所謂達德焉者夫子嘗
以之自道矣然則學者果何所入邪中庸曰好
學近乎知力行近乎仁知恥近乎勇此又入德
之事也從事於斯則知如大舜仁如顏子勇如
子路之所聞者亦可幾矣此固夫子屢言之意
也有志者其念諸
詩曰在彼無惡在此無射庶幾夙夜以永
punctuated:
憂者，必其仁之未至也。夫惟仁焉，理之純乎天而不雜以人者，復還於我矣。順理則裕，無愆於志也；隨寓而安，無動於中也。理以勝天下之私，而物欲之累非所患矣，夫何憂？至若仁知合一，而勇以強之，斯學之全也。然勇有未至，則懼心生矣。夫惟勇焉，浩然之氣善養其初，天德之剛克全於我，則見義必為，當大任不動其心也；自反而縮，遇事變不喪其守也。中有所主，而外無所慮矣，何懼之有邪？是知不惑則知至而道以明，不憂則仁至而道以行，不懼則勇之至而道亦無不強矣。學者可不驗吾學之所至，而求以造其極哉？抑是道也，即所謂達德焉者，夫子嘗以之自道矣。然則學者果何所入邪？《中庸》曰：「好學近乎知，力行近乎仁，知恥近乎勇。」此又入德之事也。從事於斯，則知如大舜，仁如顏子，勇如子路之所聞者，亦可幾矣。此固夫子屢言之意也，有志者其念諸！

《詩》曰：「在彼無惡，在此無射。庶幾夙夜，以永
translation_en:
…have worries must be those whose benevolence has not yet reached perfection. Only through benevolence does principle, purely of Heaven and unmixed with human selfishness, return to oneself. Following principle, one is at ease, with no fault in one’s intentions; content wherever one finds oneself, one remains unperturbed within. Principle overcomes all selfishness under Heaven, and the encumbrances of material desire cease to be a concern. What worry can there be? When benevolence and wisdom unite, and courage strengthens them, learning is complete. Yet if courage has not reached perfection, fear arises. Only through courage, with the vast, flowing vital energy well nurtured from its beginnings, can the strength of Heaven’s virtue be fully realized in oneself. Then, seeing what is right, one invariably acts, undertaking great responsibilities without being shaken in heart; examining oneself and finding oneself upright, one encounters changing circumstances without abandoning one’s steadfast principles. With a firm guiding commitment within, one has no anxieties about what lies outside. What is there to fear? Thus we know that freedom from perplexity means wisdom has reached perfection and the Way is thereby illuminated; freedom from worry means benevolence has reached perfection and the Way is thereby practiced; freedom from fear means courage has reached perfection and the Way, too, is upheld with strength in every respect. Can learners fail to examine how far their learning has advanced and seek to reach its utmost height?

Moreover, this Way is precisely what is meant by the universally applicable virtues, with which the Master once described himself. Where, then, should learners actually begin? The Doctrine of the Mean says: “To love learning is to approach wisdom; to practice earnestly is to approach benevolence; to know shame is to approach courage.” These, in turn, are the practices through which one enters into virtue. By devoting oneself to them, one may hope to approach wisdom like that of the great Shun, benevolence like that of Master Yan, and courage such as Zilu heard taught. This is indeed the intent of the Master’s repeated statements. Let those with aspiration ponder it!

The Book of Odes says: “There, let there be no hatred of you; here, let there be no weariness of you. Strive, morning and night, thereby forever to…”

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
終譽君子未有不如此而蚤有譽於天下
者也
同考試官教諭張　批〔引詩證君子六事兼備乃可得譽作者類多失古此篇上下文意有照應有歸宿當是作手敬羡敬羡〕
劉敏政
考試官學正王　批〔詞不煩而意自盡〕
考試官教授許　批〔未有不如此處就題發揮得子思口氣〕
===
中庸引詩以明王制盡善而後有聞於世也夫
王者備衆善而天下之譽歸之否則見其無聞
也已中庸二十九章承上章居上不驕而言以
發明人道意謂君子制作之盡善而能致天下
之順治者不觀之於詩乎彼振鷺之詩有曰在
彼無惡在此無射庶幾夙夜以永終譽蓋言名
譽之來由於人心之孚則君子之致譽可知矣
是故王天下之君子必操三重之權備六事之
善而後可以服天下之人心固也若夫不知而
punctuated:
終譽。君子未有不如此而蚤有譽於天下者也。
同考試官教諭張，批〔引詩證君子六事兼備乃可得譽，作者類多失古。此篇上下文意有照應，有歸宿，當是作手。敬羡，敬羡。〕
劉敏政
考試官學正王，批〔詞不煩而意自盡。〕
考試官教授許，批〔未有不如此處，就題發揮，得子思口氣。〕
中庸引詩以明王制盡善而後有聞於世也。夫王者備衆善而天下之譽歸之，否則見其無聞也已。中庸二十九章承上章居上不驕而言，以發明人道，意謂君子制作之盡善而能致天下之順治者，不觀之於詩乎？彼振鷺之詩有曰：「在彼無惡，在此無射，庶幾夙夜，以永終譽。」蓋言名譽之來，由於人心之孚，則君子之致譽可知矣。是故王天下之君子必操三重之權，備六事之善，而後可以服天下之人心，固也。若夫不知而
translation_en:
…preserve his good name forever to the end. Never has a gentleman gained an early reputation throughout the realm without acting in this way.
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔The quotation from the Odes demonstrates that a gentleman can gain a good reputation only when all six requirements are fulfilled. Writers commonly miss the ancient meaning. In this essay, the ideas in the earlier and later passages correspond and reach a definite conclusion. Its author must be an accomplished writer. Admirable, admirable!〕
Liu Minzheng.
Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The wording is concise, yet the meaning is fully expressed.〕
Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: 〔At “Never … without acting in this way,” the exposition develops the set topic and captures Zisi’s tone.〕
The Doctrine of the Mean quotes the Odes to show that a king’s institutions must attain complete excellence before he gains renown in the world. When a king possesses every excellence, the praise of all under Heaven comes to him; otherwise, he will simply remain without renown. Chapter twenty-nine of the Doctrine of the Mean continues from the preceding chapter’s statement about occupying a high position without arrogance, elucidating the human Way. Its meaning is this: should we not look to the Odes to see how the gentleman’s establishment of institutions attains complete excellence and thereby brings the realm into harmonious order? The ode “Egrets in Flight” says: “There he is not hated; here he occasions no weariness. May he, morning and night, preserve his good name forever to the end.” This means that reputation comes from winning people’s trust; thus we can understand how the gentleman gains praise.
Therefore, the gentleman who rules all under Heaven must wield authority over the three weighty matters and fulfill the six requirements of excellence before he can win the hearts of everyone in the realm. This is certain. As for one who, without understanding, …

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
作之者人極欲立而範圍或繆其方所謂本諸
身徵諸民合前聖於既往者未能也王制欲修
而裁化弗妙其用所謂參天地質鬼神契後聖
於將來者未能也將見禮不足以為節度不足
以為式文不足以為書法雖立也行有戾乎人
情民將有弗信者矣何以垂悠久之則政雖施
也動必乖乎物理民將有弗從者矣何以協遠
近之歸求寡過於天下不可得也又豈有不善
其道而享天下之譽者哉是必居王者之位行
===
王者之道定王者之業君子之能事畢矣嗟夫
唐虞三代遠矣時至戰國功力相尚非無制作
也率不能修德凝道以為之本無怪乎治之不
善而譽之無聞也子思有憂于此而反復言之
其垂訓後世之意亦可謂詳且切矣居上者盍
鑒之哉
其為氣也至大至剛以直養而無害則塞
于天地之間
王嘉言
punctuated:
作之者，人極欲立，而範圍或繆其方，所謂本諸身、徵諸民、合前聖於既往者，未能也；王制欲修，而裁化弗妙其用，所謂參天地、質鬼神、契後聖於將來者，未能也。將見禮不足以為節，度不足以為式，文不足以為書。法雖立也，行有戾乎人情，民將有弗信者矣，何以垂悠久之則？政雖施也，動必乖乎物理，民將有弗從者矣，何以協遠近之歸？求寡過於天下，不可得也。又豈有不善其道而享天下之譽者哉？是必居王者之位，行王者之道，定王者之業，君子之能事畢矣。嗟夫！唐虞三代遠矣！時至戰國，功力相尚，非無制作也，率不能修德凝道以為之本，無怪乎治之不善而譽之無聞也。子思有憂于此而反復言之，其垂訓後世之意，亦可謂詳且切矣。居上者盍鑒之哉？

其為氣也，至大至剛，以直養而無害，則塞于天地之間。

王嘉言
translation_en:
…those who institute them: they wish to establish the supreme standard for human conduct, yet their way of giving it form and bounds may be mistaken. They cannot accomplish what is meant by rooting it in their own persons, verifying it among the people, and bringing it into accord with the sages of the past. They wish to perfect royal institutions, yet fail to give subtle efficacy to their ordering and transforming work. They cannot accomplish what is meant by aligning them with Heaven and Earth, testing them against ghosts and spirits, and bringing them into accord with sages yet to come. Thus their rites will prove inadequate as restraints, their measures inadequate as models, and their written forms inadequate as a standard for writing. Though laws are established, their implementation runs counter to human feelings, and some among the people will not trust them. How, then, can they bequeath enduring standards? Though policies are put into effect, their every action necessarily conflicts with the principles of things, and some among the people will not obey them. How, then, can they unite the allegiance of those near and far? They cannot hope to commit few errors in governing all under Heaven. And how could anyone whose Way is not good enjoy the praise of all under Heaven? One must occupy the position of a true king, practice the Way of a true king, and establish the achievements of a true king. Only then are the noble man's capacities fully realized.

Alas! The ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun and of the Three Dynasties are far distant! By the Warring States period, men vied in esteeming achievement and force. It was not that they instituted nothing, but that they generally failed to cultivate virtue and consolidate the Way as their foundation. No wonder their government was poor and no praise of them was heard. Zisi was troubled by this and spoke of it repeatedly. His intention to leave instruction for later generations may indeed be called both thorough and earnest. Should not those in high positions take warning from it?

“As qi, it is supremely great and supremely firm. If nourished with uprightness and left unharmed, it fills the space between Heaven and Earth.”

Wang Jiayan.

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導佘　批〔浩然之氣形容殆盡錄之〕
同考試官教諭趙　批〔能說出充塞意〕
同考試官教諭馬　批〔有關鍵有思致可取〕
考試官學正王　批〔體認真切〕
考試官教授許　批〔其氣亦似浩然者〕
大賢論氣本體之盛善養之則充矣夫浩然之
氣人得于天地者也苟有以養之斯充塞而無
間矣孟子舉其長於告子者以答公孫丑及此
若謂存乎人者不動心非難而養氣爲難浩然
===
之氣雖未易以言語形容矣然其本體之實亦
有可言者焉何則陰陽變化神無不合吾萃其
精英以爲四體之充雖曰有形而不依于形其
諸一元之充滿者乎何至大也五氣交感化無
不宣吾得其醇一以爲此志之輔雖曰有物而
不囿于物其諸大造之直遂者邪何至剛也夫
是氣也人皆有之病于弗求戕于欲速者衆矣
誠能自反而縮務去乎梏亡之害俟其自得不
參以作爲之私如是則至大不蔽其量至剛不
punctuated:
同考試官訓導佘　批〔浩然之氣形容殆盡，錄之。〕
同考試官教諭趙　批〔能說出充塞意。〕
同考試官教諭馬　批〔有關鍵，有思致，可取。〕
考試官學正王　批〔體認真切。〕
考試官教授許　批〔其氣亦似浩然者。〕

大賢論氣本體之盛，善養之則充矣。夫浩然之氣，人得于天地者也。苟有以養之，斯充塞而無間矣。孟子舉其長於告子者以答公孫丑，及此，若謂存乎人者，不動心非難，而養氣爲難。浩然之氣，雖未易以言語形容矣，然其本體之實，亦有可言者焉。何則？陰陽變化，神無不合，吾萃其精英以爲四體之充。雖曰有形，而不依于形，其諸一元之充滿者乎？何至大也！五氣交感，化無不宣，吾得其醇一以爲此志之輔。雖曰有物，而不囿于物，其諸大造之直遂者邪？何至剛也！夫是氣也，人皆有之，病于弗求、戕于欲速者衆矣。誠能自反而縮，務去乎梏亡之害，俟其自得，不參以作爲之私，如是則至大不蔽其量，至剛不
translation_en:
Associate Examiner She, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The vast, flowing vital energy is described almost exhaustively. Include this answer.”
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “It succeeds in expressing the idea of filling all space.”
Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: “It has a pivotal argument and thoughtful refinement; it merits selection.”
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “Its understanding is authentic and incisive.”
Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: “The energy of this writing, too, seems vast and flowing.”

The great worthy discusses the fullness of vital energy in its fundamental constitution: nourish it well, and it will fill all space. Now, the vast, flowing vital energy is what human beings receive from Heaven and Earth. If one has the means to nourish it, it will fill all space without a gap. In answering Gongsun Chou, Mengzi mentioned the respect in which he surpassed Gaozi and came to this point. It was as though he were saying: Among the things that lie within oneself, keeping the mind unmoved is not difficult; nourishing vital energy is difficult. Although this vast, flowing vital energy is not readily described in words, something can nevertheless be said about the reality of its fundamental constitution. Why is this?

As yin and yang transform, their numinous operation unites with everything. I gather their finest essence to fill my four limbs. Though it is said to possess form, it does not depend upon form. Is it not the fullness of the single primordial force? How supremely great it is! As the five vital energies interact, their transforming power extends everywhere. I receive their purity and unity to support this will of mine. Though it is said to have substance, it is not confined by material things. Is it not the unimpeded advance of the great creative process? How supremely firm it is!

Everyone possesses this vital energy, yet many impair it by failing to seek it, or injure it through a desire for speedy results. If one can truly examine oneself and find oneself upright, strive to remove the harm caused by fettering and losing it, await its spontaneous attainment, and introduce no selfishness through contrived effort, then its supreme greatness will suffer no restriction of its capacity, and its supreme firmness will not …

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
虧其體天地之絪緼而磅礴者吾氣之經緯錯
綜也始非有合終非有離矣蓋天下莫能載焉
乾坤之混闢而妙合者吾氣之周流變通也此
非有餘彼非不足矣蓋天下莫能破焉夫浩然
之氣塞于天地亦存乎所養我之長於告子如
斯而已矣豈以御相霸王動其心乎嗟夫孟子
之養氣知言雖有攸屬而實則察乎性命之間
非二物也惟其賦生之初純駁不齊是以不能
盡性而知命告子之義外公都子善不善之性
橫議天下甚則萘儀秦之勢以為大丈夫豈所
謂當大任而不動心者邪故嘗謂孟子之道大
於性善精於存心而歸其極于知言養氣之旨
知斯三者而後有以見其學孔之志配禹之功
矣
易
王假有廟致孝享也
吳三樂
同考試官教諭劉 批〔易義明潔如此作者蓋〕
punctuated:
虧其體，天地之絪緼而磅礴者，吾氣之經緯錯綜也。始非有合，終非有離矣，蓋天下莫能載焉。乾坤之混闢而妙合者，吾氣之周流變通也。此非有餘，彼非不足矣，蓋天下莫能破焉。夫浩然之氣塞于天地，亦存乎所養。我之長於告子，如斯而已矣，豈以御相霸王動其心乎？嗟夫！孟子之養氣知言，雖有攸屬，而實則察乎性命之間，非二物也。惟其賦生之初，純駁不齊，是以不能盡性而知命。告子之義外、公都子善不善之性，橫議天下，甚則萘儀秦之勢以為大丈夫，豈所謂當大任而不動心者邪？故嘗謂孟子之道，大於性善，精於存心，而歸其極于知言養氣之旨。知斯三者，而後有以見其學孔之志、配禹之功矣。
易
王假有廟，致孝享也。
吳三樂
同考試官教諭劉，批〔易義明潔如此，作者蓋〕
translation_en:
…diminish its substance. The intermingling and boundless expansiveness of Heaven and Earth are the interwoven workings of my vital force. At the beginning there was no joining; at the end there is no separation. Nothing under Heaven can contain it. The undifferentiated unity, opening forth, and wondrous conjunction of Heaven and Earth are the circulation and transformations of my vital force. Here there is no surplus; there there is no deficiency. Nothing under Heaven can break it. That the vast, flowing vital force fills Heaven and Earth depends upon how it is nourished. My superiority to Gaozi lies in this alone. How could holding ministerial office or attaining hegemony or kingship disturb my heart?
Alas! Although Mencius’s nourishing of vital force and understanding of words each has its own concern, in truth both involve discerning human nature and Heaven’s mandate; they are not two separate things. It is only because the endowments received at birth differ in purity and admixture that people cannot fully realize their nature and understand Heaven’s mandate. Gaozi’s claim that righteousness is external and Gongduzi’s discussion of good and evil in human nature spread as wayward doctrines throughout the world. Worse still, some invoke [?] the power of Zhang Yi and Su Qin as the mark of a great man. Could these be what is meant by those who shoulder great responsibilities without their hearts being moved? Thus I have long said that the breadth of Mencius’s Way lies in the goodness of human nature, its refinement in preserving the heart, and its ultimate culmination in the purport of understanding words and nourishing vital force. Only by understanding these three aspects can one perceive his resolve to emulate Confucius and his achievement that matched Yu’s.
Book of Changes
“The king comes to his ancestral temple”: this means offering sacrifice with utmost filial devotion.
Wu Sanle
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔With an interpretation of the Changes so lucid and clear, the author surely…〕

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
不多見
同考試官教諭辛　批〔氣昌辭　整可嘉〕
考試官學正王　批〔知萃道者〕
考試官教授許　批〔縝密雅健〕
人君臨奉先之所盡饗親之誠夫誠以饗親孝
子之行也王者至廟而能致之此世道所以萃
也與萃之彖有曰王假有廟夫子彖傳申之以
為昔者明王以孝治天下也必本於自盡其見
諸行事也恒慎于祭義是故為之宮室以依祖
===
考之神設其宗祧以叙昭穆之統斯固王者之
有廟矣當聚之時猶必在中而蒞夫祀事者豈
徒然哉誠以祖功宗德昊天罔極大業洪圖萬
世永賴報本追遠之心可但已乎慮事以豫具
物以周于時對越而致其慤焉吾之孚信與先
王之精神相為流通真若有以聞乎容聲歎息
者矣禮樂以叙百官以備于時奠獻而致其愛
焉吾之志意與祖考之神明相為感格真若有
以見其嗜欲居處者矣夫王者至廟以致孝如
punctuated:
不多見。
同考試官教諭辛，批〔氣昌辭　整可嘉〕
考試官學正王，批〔知萃道者〕
考試官教授許，批〔縝密雅健〕
人君臨奉先之所，盡饗親之誠。夫誠以饗親，孝子之行也。王者至廟而能致之，此世道所以萃也與！萃之彖有曰：「王假有廟。」夫子彖傳申之，以為：昔者明王以孝治天下也，必本於自盡，其見諸行事也，恒慎于祭義。是故為之宮室，以依祖考之神；設其宗祧，以叙昭穆之統。斯固王者之有廟矣。當聚之時，猶必在中而蒞夫祀事者，豈徒然哉？誠以祖功宗德，昊天罔極；大業洪圖，萬世永賴。報本追遠之心，可但已乎？慮事以豫，具物以周，于時對越而致其慤焉。吾之孚信與先王之精神相為流通，真若有以聞乎容聲歎息者矣。禮樂以叙，百官以備，于時奠獻而致其愛焉。吾之志意與祖考之神明相為感格，真若有以見其嗜欲居處者矣。夫王者至廟以致孝如
translation_en:
…are seldom encountered.
Associate Examiner Xin, Instructor, comments: “Abundant vitality and orderly diction: commendable.”
Examiner Wang, School Director, comments: “One who understands the Way of Gathering.”
Examiner Xu, Prefectural School Professor, comments: “Meticulous, elegant, and vigorous.”
The ruler comes to the place where his ancestors are served and fully expresses his sincerity in offering to his forebears. To offer to one’s forebears with sincerity is the conduct of a filial son. When a king arrives at the ancestral temple and can give full expression to this, surely this is what brings the world into unity! The Judgment of Gathering states: “The king comes to his ancestral temple.” The Master elaborates upon this in his Commentary on the Judgment, meaning that when the enlightened kings of antiquity governed the realm through filial piety, they necessarily grounded this in exerting themselves to the utmost. In putting this into practice, they were always attentive to the meaning of sacrifice. Thus they built halls to house the spirits of their ancestors and established ancestral shrines to order the lineage according to the alternating zhao and mu generations. This, indeed, is what it means for a king to possess an ancestral temple. At a time of gathering, he must still occupy the center [?] and preside over the sacrifices. Could this be without purpose?
Truly, the achievements and virtues of his ancestors are boundless as the vast heavens; their great undertaking and grand design sustain ten thousand generations forever. Could the impulse to repay one’s origins and remember distant ancestors simply cease? He plans the proceedings beforehand and fully prepares the offerings; then, reverently facing the spirits, he expresses his utmost sincerity. His good faith communicates with the spirits of the former kings, just as though he could hear their bearing, voices, and sighs [?]. Ritual and music are arranged in order, and the officials are all in attendance; then, in presenting the offerings, he expresses his utmost love. His intentions and thoughts resonate with the numinous spirits of his ancestors, just as though he could see their tastes and desires, their dwelling and daily life. Now, when the king comes to the ancestral temple and expresses his filial piety in such…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
此是以上獲神眷而福無不受下攝衆志而人
無不和萃天下之道豈有加於此哉或曰萃以
假廟渙以立廟時異而事同何也於戲此聖王
制禮之精義治國如視掌者豈易言哉蓋天人
一道幽明一理明德之馨足以動天地感鬼神
況民物乎以萃則益聚以渙則合散百世以俟
聖人而不惑也夫祀國之大事有事于祀典者
尚鑒於斯
===
易之爲書也不可遠爲道也屢遷變動不
居周流六虛上下無常剛柔相易不可爲
典要惟變所適
陸柬
同考試官教諭劉　批〔屢遷以下多不能體認此〕
篇直造精微蓋讀易而有得者錄之
同考試官教諭辛　批〔易義能體認發揮無疵者〕
考試官學正王　批〔屢遷處明徹〕
考試官教授許　批〔殆亦不遠易者〕
大傳論易切于人必詳其道之變者以見之也
punctuated:
此，是以上獲神眷，而福無不受；下攝衆志，而人無不和。萃天下之道，豈有加於此哉？或曰：「萃以假廟，渙以立廟，時異而事同，何也？」於戲！此聖王制禮之精義，治國如視掌者，豈易言哉？蓋天人一道，幽明一理，明德之馨足以動天地、感鬼神，況民物乎？以萃則益聚，以渙則合散，百世以俟聖人而不惑也。夫祀，國之大事，有事于祀典者，尚鑒於斯。

易之爲書也，不可遠；爲道也，屢遷，變動不居，周流六虛，上下無常，剛柔相易，不可爲典要，惟變所適。

陸柬

同考試官教諭劉，批〔屢遷以下，多不能體認。此〕篇直造精微，蓋讀易而有得者，錄之。

同考試官教諭辛，批〔易義能體認發揮，無疵者。〕

考試官學正王，批〔屢遷處明徹。〕

考試官教授許，批〔殆亦不遠易者。〕

大傳論易切于人，必詳其道之變者，以見之也。
translation_en:
…in this manner. Thus, above, he wins the spirits’ favor and receives every blessing; below, he draws together the people’s wills, and all are harmonious. Could any way of gathering all under Heaven surpass this? Someone asks: “In Gathering, the king approaches the ancestral temple; in Dispersion, he establishes the ancestral temple. The circumstances differ, yet the undertaking is the same. Why?” Ah! This is the profound meaning of the sage kings’ institution of ritual, by which governing the state becomes as clear as looking at one’s palm. How could it be easily explained? Heaven and humanity follow one Way; the unseen and visible realms share one principle. The fragrance of luminous virtue suffices to move Heaven and Earth and stir ghosts and spirits—how much more the people and other beings! In Gathering, it increases their unity; in Dispersion, it reunites the scattered. One may await a sage a hundred generations hence without doubt about this. Sacrifice is a great affair of state. May those responsible for the sacrificial institutions take this as their mirror.

“As a book, the Changes must not be kept at a distance. As a Way, it shifts repeatedly, changing and moving without rest, circulating through the six empty positions. Its ascent and descent are inconstant; the firm and yielding exchange places. It cannot be made into a fixed standard: it follows wherever change leads.”

Lu Jian 陸柬

Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “From ‘shifts repeatedly’ onward, most fail to grasp the meaning fully. This essay reaches directly into its subtle depths. Its author has evidently gained insight from reading the Changes. Select it.”

Associate Examiner Xin, Instructor, comments: “An essay that grasps and develops the meaning of the Changes without flaw.”

Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: “The treatment of ‘shifts repeatedly’ is lucid and penetrating.”

Examiner Xu, Prefectural School Professor, comments: “He, too, is surely one who does not keep the Changes at a distance.”

When the Great Commentary discusses how closely the Changes concerns human beings, it necessarily explains in detail the transformations of its Way in order to demonstrate this.

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
夫變易以從道易書之體要也知乎此則所以
不可遠者思過半矣夫子示人以學易如此蓋
謂聖人之作易也開物成務百姓之愚咸以與
其能極深研幾萬物之情靡不彰其類其爲書
也蓋有不可須臾遠者矣嘗自其道之屢遷者
觀之易有卦爻所以極賾效動也推行不倚于
一隅易貢不屬于方體何莫而非陰陽之變動
乎卦有六位所以稽實待虛也乘承而無專質
比應而無定名何莫而非陰陽之周流乎自內
===
而外則賤乘乎貴由悔而貞則遠取乎近一上
一下有常分而無常運矣進極而退則陽居乎
陰消極而長則老交于少一剛一柔有定體而
無定用矣是蓋隨機裁化不可以一時之宜而
索設卦之蘊變之所適道亦寓焉趨時致變不
可以一事之利而明觀象之故情之所遷理亦
至焉吁至一者天下之理也至變者易書之妙
也非一則不能神化以盡情非變則不能會通
以盡言茲其所以不可遠也與雖然天生神物
punctuated: 夫變易以從道，易書之體要也。知乎此，則所以不可遠者，思過半矣。夫子示人以學易如此，蓋謂聖人之作易也，開物成務，百姓之愚咸以與其能；極深研幾，萬物之情靡不彰其類。其爲書也，蓋有不可須臾遠者矣。嘗自其道之屢遷者觀之：易有卦爻，所以極賾效動也。推行不倚于一隅，易貢不屬于方體，何莫而非陰陽之變動乎？卦有六位，所以稽實待虛也。乘承而無專質，比應而無定名，何莫而非陰陽之周流乎？自內而外，則賤乘乎貴；由悔而貞，則遠取乎近。一上一下，有常分而無常運矣。進極而退，則陽居乎陰；消極而長，則老交于少。一剛一柔，有定體而無定用矣。是蓋隨機裁化，不可以一時之宜而索設卦之蘊；變之所適，道亦寓焉。趨時致變，不可以一事之利而明觀象之故；情之所遷，理亦至焉。吁！至一者，天下之理也；至變者，易書之妙也。非一，則不能神化以盡情；非變，則不能會通以盡言。茲其所以不可遠也與！雖然，天生神物，
translation_en: Now, changing in order to accord with the Way is the essential substance of the Book of Changes. Understanding this takes one more than halfway toward understanding why it must never be kept at a distance. This is how the Master taught people to study the Changes. His meaning was that, when the sages composed the Changes, they disclosed the nature of things and brought affairs to completion, enabling even the ignorant among the common people to share in their capacities. They plumbed the depths and investigated the incipient signs of change, revealing the dispositions of all things according to their kinds. As a book, it must therefore never be kept at a distance, even for a moment. Consider it in terms of the repeated shifts of its Way. The Changes has hexagrams and lines through which to fathom the mysterious and represent movement. Its operation is not confined to one quarter, and its workings [?] are not bound to any direction or form. What among these is not the changing movement of yin and yang? A hexagram has six positions through which to examine what is filled and await what is empty. In riding upon or supporting one another, the lines have no exclusive character; in adjacency or correspondence, they have no fixed designation. What among these is not the circulation of yin and yang? Moving from the inner trigram to the outer, the lowly rides above the noble; moving from the outer trigram, hui, to the inner, zhen, the distant draws upon the near. Now above, now below: there are constant distinctions of position, but no constant course of movement. When advance reaches its utmost and turns to retreat, yang occupies the place of yin; when decline reaches its utmost and turns to growth, the old interchanges with the young. Now firm, now yielding: there are definite forms, but no fixed functions. Thus transformations are shaped according to the occasion; one cannot fathom the profundity of the establishment of the hexagrams through what is fitting at a single moment. Wherever change proceeds, the Way also resides. Change is brought about in accordance with the time; one cannot understand the grounds for contemplating the images through what is advantageous in a single affair. Wherever circumstances shift, principle also reaches. Ah! What is supremely one is the principle of all under Heaven; what is supremely changeable is the subtlety of the Book of Changes. Without unity, there could be no numinous transformation that fully encompasses the dispositions of things; without change, there could be no comprehensive interconnection that fully encompasses what can be expressed. Is this not why it must never be kept at a distance? Nevertheless, Heaven produces numinous things…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
圖書是陳易之原也知來藏往神武不殺易之
體也利用出入民咸用之裁于上而效于下蓍
也是故有忠信之事則可以卜筮具神明之德
則可以作易故曰苟非其人道不虛行或者乃
以畸贅晝夜自謂足以明易而不知其道之不
能變也噫
書
監于先王成憲其永無愆
劉敏政
===
同考試官教諭張　批〔寫出法祖意僅見此篇〕
考試官學正王　批〔簡明〕
考試官教授許　批〔講法祖無愆處親切得〕
老臣忠愛之意
大臣告賢王以法祖之有益所以揭為學之準
也蓋前人之法後人之鑑也守之將無不善矣
大臣論學而以是歸之宜哉傅說告高宗及此
若謂人君非務學無以通古之道非法祖無以
適今之宜吾王既典學而德修矣可不以先王
punctuated:
圖書是陳，易之原也；知來藏往，神武不殺，易之體也。利用出入，民咸用之，裁于上而效于下，蓍也。是故有忠信之事，則可以卜筮；具神明之德，則可以作易。故曰：「苟非其人，道不虛行。」或者乃以畸贅晝夜，自謂足以明易，而不知其道之不能變也。噫！
書
監于先王成憲，其永無愆。
劉敏政
同考試官教諭張　批〔寫出法祖意僅見此篇〕
考試官學正王　批〔簡明〕
考試官教授許　批〔講法祖無愆處親切得〕老臣忠愛之意。
大臣告賢王以法祖之有益，所以揭為學之準也。蓋前人之法，後人之鑑也，守之將無不善矣。大臣論學而以是歸之，宜哉！傅說告高宗及此，若謂人君非務學無以通古之道，非法祖無以適今之宜。吾王既典學而德修矣，可不以先王
translation_en:
…The Chart and the Writing are displayed: these are the origins of the Changes. Knowing what is to come and storing up what has passed, possessing divine martial power without killing: these are the essential character of the Changes. Making their use beneficial in going out and coming in, so that all the people employ them, with judgments made above and effects realized below—such is the work of the milfoil stalks. Thus, where an undertaking is marked by loyalty and trustworthiness, one may divine by tortoise shell and milfoil; possessing the virtue of spiritual illumination, one may compose the Changes. Hence it is said: “Unless there is the right person, the Way does not operate of itself.” Yet some treat day and night as superfluous appendages [?], claiming that this suffices to elucidate the Changes, without realizing that their way cannot accommodate change. Alas!

Book of Documents
“Take as your mirror the established statutes of the former kings, and you will forever be without fault.”
Liu Minzheng

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Only this essay brings out the meaning of emulating the ancestors.〕
Examiner Wang, Director of Studies, comments: 〔Concise and clear.〕
Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: 〔Its explanation of how emulating the ancestors brings freedom from fault is apt and captures〕 the old minister’s loyal and loving intent.

A great minister tells a worthy king of the benefits of emulating his ancestors, thereby setting this forth as the standard for learning. The laws of earlier men are the mirror of those who come after them; by observing these laws, nothing will fail to be good. How fitting that the great minister, in discussing learning, should make this his conclusion! When Fu Yue spoke to Gaozong on this subject, it was as though he said: “Unless a ruler devotes himself to learning, he cannot comprehend the Way of antiquity; unless he emulates his ancestors, he cannot meet the needs of the present. My king has already steadfastly pursued learning and cultivated his virtue. Can he fail to take the former kings…”

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
之法為監乎蓋先王以建中之聖而謨訓有可
師以垂統之君而典刑為當守必祖武是繩視
其所以修身者而修身即昧爽丕顯之謨以求
成德之允恊也攸行是率視其所以治人者而
治人即克綏厥猷之典以求明哲之作則也若
是則何過之有哉蓋道涉于多岐而我失其定
據欲免過也難矣今所法者聖祖則有所持循
而將止於至善所守者貽謀則不事紛更而自
合乎大猷以之修已則台德以立足以紹齊聖
===
之懿率舊章而不忘也以之治人則兆民以康
足以繼輯寧之化訓成式于永乂也夫如是則
學有實用而非徒學矣王其以是務乎大抵創
業之君理天下也至周憂天下也至悉而其所
以慮後世也至遠世守其法雖萬世存可也繼
世賢君欲大有為于天下亦必守祖宗之法而
勵精以圖之將與古先哲王並美焉不然吾恐
叢脞之多患也伊尹之于太甲傅說之于高宗
言則必稱先王者眞深長之慮哉
punctuated:
之法為監乎？蓋先王以建中之聖，而謨訓有可師；以垂統之君，而典刑為當守。必祖武是繩，視其所以修身者而修身，即昧爽丕顯之謨，以求成德之允恊也；攸行是率，視其所以治人者而治人，即克綏厥猷之典，以求明哲之作則也。若是，則何過之有哉？蓋道涉于多岐，而我失其定據，欲免過也難矣。今所法者聖祖，則有所持循，而將止於至善；所守者貽謀，則不事紛更，而自合乎大猷。以之修已，則台德以立，足以紹齊聖之懿，率舊章而不忘也；以之治人，則兆民以康，足以繼輯寧之化，訓成式于永乂也。夫如是，則學有實用，而非徒學矣。王其以是務乎！
大抵創業之君，理天下也至周，憂天下也至悉，而其所以慮後世也至遠。世守其法，雖萬世存可也。繼世賢君，欲大有為于天下，亦必守祖宗之法，而勵精以圖之，將與古先哲王並美焉。不然，吾恐叢脞之多患也。伊尹之于太甲，傅說之于高宗，言則必稱先王者，眞深長之慮哉！
translation_en:
…take the former kings’ standards as your mirror? The former king was a sage who established the mean, and his counsels and instructions offer models to emulate; he was a ruler who handed down the succession, and his established precedents must be preserved. You must follow your ancestor’s footsteps: cultivate yourself by observing how he cultivated himself, following his counsel to make virtue greatly manifest from daybreak, so that your perfected virtue may truly accord with his. Take his conduct as your guide: govern others by observing how he governed others, following his precedent of bringing peace through his Way, so that your wisdom and discernment may serve as a model. If you do this, what errors could there be? When the Way branches into many paths and we lose our firm point of reference, avoiding error is difficult indeed. Now, if the model you follow is your sage ancestor, you will have something to adhere to and will come to rest in the highest good. If what you preserve is the counsel he bequeathed, you will avoid incessant alterations and naturally accord with the great Way. Apply this to cultivating yourself, and your virtue will be established: you will be able to carry forward the excellence of his enlightened sagacity, following the old statutes without forgetting them. Apply it to governing others, and the myriad people will enjoy peace: you will be able to continue his work of bringing harmony and tranquillity, following established models to secure lasting order. Thus learning will have practical application and will be more than mere learning. May Your Majesty devote yourself to this!
In general, a founding ruler is utterly comprehensive in ordering the realm, thoroughly attentive in his concern for it, and far-reaching in his consideration for later generations. If successive generations preserve his standards, the dynasty can endure even for ten thousand generations. A worthy ruler who inherits the throne and wishes to accomplish great things in the realm must likewise preserve his ancestors’ standards and exert himself wholeheartedly to realize his aims. He will then rival the sage kings of antiquity in excellence. Otherwise, I fear the many troubles that arise from preoccupation with petty details. Whenever Yi Yin spoke to Tai Jia, or Fu Yue to Gaozong, they invariably invoked the former kings. How profound and far-reaching their concern truly was!

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
乃命三后恤功于民伯夷降典折民惟刑
禹平水土主名山川稷降播種農植嘉穀
三后成功惟殷於民
祝永順
同考試官教諭張　批〔通篇脫去陳腐而詞語款暢體裁峻整精神束處猶有思致可謂明經之士矣〕
考試官學正王　批〔得訓刑意〕
考試官教授許　批〔雅健〕
聖君命群臣有為于天下則事治而民阜矣蓋
===
君得臣而後功可立也此帝舜憂民之功所以
必資於三后歟昔穆王訓刑首述帝舜之事以
為昔帝舜之遏苗民也既清問以得民之情又
敷德以動民之化然豈止於是而已邪蓋知治
世以安民為本而成功以任賢為急故既咨伯
夷復命禹稷使各致其憂民之功焉當是時也
民之所可憂者詛盟之習尚在昏墊之患未除
而阻饑之戹未已也伯夷則典三禮以息其邪
說播五刑以齊其未化禹度土功而封表山川
punctuated:
乃命三后，恤功于民。伯夷降典，折民惟刑；禹平水土，主名山川；稷降播種，農植嘉穀。三后成功，惟殷於民。
祝永順
同考試官教諭張　批〔通篇脫去陳腐，而詞語款暢，體裁峻整，精神束處猶有思致，可謂明經之士矣。〕
考試官學正王　批〔得訓刑意。〕
考試官教授許　批〔雅健。〕
聖君命群臣有為于天下，則事治而民阜矣。蓋君得臣而後功可立也，此帝舜憂民之功所以必資於三后歟？昔穆王訓刑，首述帝舜之事，以為昔帝舜之遏苗民也，既清問以得民之情，又敷德以動民之化，然豈止於是而已邪？蓋知治世以安民為本，而成功以任賢為急，故既咨伯夷，復命禹稷，使各致其憂民之功焉。當是時也，民之所可憂者，詛盟之習尚在，昏墊之患未除，而阻饑之戹未已也。伯夷則典三禮以息其邪說，播五刑以齊其未化；禹度土功而封表山川
translation_en:
“He then commanded the three lords to labor with concern for the people. Bo Yi promulgated the statutes, correcting the people through punishments. Yu brought the waters and lands into order and presided over the naming of mountains and rivers. Ji disseminated methods of sowing, cultivating and planting fine grains. The three lords accomplished their work, richly benefiting the people.”
Zhu Yongshun
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Throughout, the essay casts off stale conventions. Its language flows easily, and its composition is rigorous and orderly. Even where its energy is drawn together, it retains thoughtful refinement. He may indeed be called a scholar who understands the Classics.〕
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔Grasps the meaning of the instructions on punishments.〕
Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: 〔Elegant and vigorous.〕
When a sage ruler commands his ministers to undertake work in the realm, affairs are brought into order and the people prosper. For only after a ruler obtains worthy ministers can achievements be established. Was this not why Emperor Shun necessarily relied on the three lords to accomplish his work of caring for the people?
In former times, when King Mu gave instructions on punishments, he began by recounting the deeds of Emperor Shun. He explained that when Emperor Shun restrained the Miao people, he made discerning inquiries to ascertain the people's circumstances and spread his virtue to bring about their transformation. Yet could his efforts have stopped there? He understood that securing the people's peace was the foundation of governing the world, and that employing worthy men was the urgent requirement for accomplishing his work. Thus, after consulting Bo Yi, he also commissioned Yu and Ji, so that each might fully accomplish his work of caring for the people.
At that time, the causes of concern for the people were that the practice of invoking curses in covenants still persisted, the scourge of inundation had not been eliminated, and the distress of hardship and famine had not ceased. Bo Yi therefore took charge of the three rites to put an end to their pernicious teachings and promulgated the five punishments to bring into line those not yet transformed. Yu planned the work upon the land and demarcated and marked the mountains and rivers…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
所以奠其居也稷教稼穡而樹藝五穀所以厚
其生也三后上承君命之重而勵翼以効其勞
下憫民命之艱而奮庸以熙其載則其功不既
成乎將見當時之民神人之典既明邪妄之俗
浸革天地平成不復巢窟以為居蔚然於咸寧
之治也蒸民乃粒不復艱食以為患熙然於九
叙之歌也其恤民之功一至是哉吁聖君命官
以憂民而民享其利如此乃有弗率其化者則
刑斯加矣茲非用刑之本邪穆王訓刑而以帝
===
舜為稱似有志於聖王之道而欲師往古之法
者然揆其中則大不然也帝舜象刑所以防姦
宄而輔民彝天下之公也穆王訓刑不過欲贖
刑聚貨以為巡遊無度之費一人之私也其所
以稱述聖王者無乃畏公議而借以自文邪然
其為言也惻然有哀矜無辜之心此孔子所以
取之歟
詩
春日遲遲卉木萋萋倉庚喈喈采蘩祁祁
punctuated:
所以奠其居也。稷教稼穡而樹藝五穀，所以厚其生也。三后上承君命之重，而勵翼以効其勞；下憫民命之艱，而奮庸以熙其載，則其功不既成乎？將見當時之民，神人之典既明，邪妄之俗浸革；天地平成，不復巢窟以為居，蔚然於咸寧之治也；蒸民乃粒，不復艱食以為患，熙然於九叙之歌也。其恤民之功一至是哉！吁！聖君命官以憂民，而民享其利如此，乃有弗率其化者，則刑斯加矣。茲非用刑之本邪？穆王訓刑而以帝舜為稱，似有志於聖王之道，而欲師往古之法者，然揆其中，則大不然也。帝舜象刑，所以防姦宄而輔民彝，天下之公也；穆王訓刑，不過欲贖刑聚貨，以為巡遊無度之費，一人之私也。其所以稱述聖王者，無乃畏公議而借以自文邪？然其為言也，惻然有哀矜無辜之心，此孔子所以取之歟？

詩

春日遲遲，卉木萋萋。倉庚喈喈，采蘩祁祁。
translation_en:
…thereby securing their dwellings. Ji taught sowing and reaping and the cultivation of the five grains, thereby enriching their livelihood. These three lords bore from above the weighty charge of their sovereign and diligently and reverently exerted themselves in his service; below, they pitied the hardships of the people's lives and applied their abilities to advance their work. Were their achievements not thus complete? One may envision the people of that time: once the prescribed relations between spirits and humans were clarified, perverse and deluded customs gradually disappeared. Heaven and earth were brought into peaceful order, and people no longer dwelt in nests or caves, flourishing under a government that brought tranquillity to all. The multitudes had grain to eat and no longer suffered from difficulty in obtaining food, joyfully singing of the nine domains brought into order. Such was the extent of their achievement in caring for the people!

Ah! The sage sovereign appointed officials to care for the people, and the people enjoyed benefits such as these. Only then, if there were those who failed to follow his transforming influence, were punishments imposed upon them. Is this not the foundation for the use of punishment? When King Mu gave his instructions on punishments and cited Emperor Shun, he appeared to aspire to the Way of the sage kings and to wish to model himself upon the methods of antiquity. Yet, when we examine his inner motives, they were very different. Emperor Shun's setting forth of punishments served to prevent wrongdoing and uphold the people's constant moral norms: this was for the common good of all under Heaven. King Mu's instructions on punishments sought merely to accumulate wealth through the redemption of punishments, to meet the expenses of his unrestrained touring: this was one man's private interest. Might he have praised and recounted the deeds of the sage kings because he feared public criticism and borrowed their example to cloak his own conduct? Nevertheless, his words convey a heartfelt compassion for the innocent. Was this why Confucius included them?

Book of Poetry

The spring days lengthen;
Plants and trees grow luxuriantly.
The orioles sing in harmony;
Those gathering white southernwood come in throngs.…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
執訊獲醜旂言還歸赫赫南仲玁狁于夷
王嘉言
同考試官訓導余　批〔能道周家勞師之意〕
同考試官教諭趙　批〔筆力駿發不枯不肤宜錄〕
同考試官教諭馬　批〔詞氣典雅得溫厚之體〕
考試官學正王　批〔森密爾雅〕
考試官教授許　批〔寫出盛時氣象〕
詩人述大將還師之樂而表其成功之大焉夫
采騁而奏凱信可樂也伐遠功成者以之不亦
===
可勞乎此勞還師之詩若謂我將帥之于征也
昔固覩雨雪而懷憂矣今其歸也不有感時而
可樂者耶是故青陽應候暄和而舒長維天時
則春矣卉木含滋蒙密而茂盛觀物態則變矣
倉庚之聲清和圓轉得氣何先也采蘩之女往
來衆多治蠶何蚤也斯時也輳門繫當訊之渠
魁行間從被獲之群醜却狄之功成矣即長途
而悠悠于邁指王國而𩤸𩤸啓行全歸之樂遂
矣是果誰之功哉乃我南仲才足以禦侮威望
punctuated:
執訊獲醜，旂言還歸。赫赫南仲，玁狁于夷。
王嘉言

同考試官教諭馬批〔詞氣典雅，得溫厚之體〕

詩人述大將還師之樂，而表其成功之大焉。夫采騁而奏凱，信可樂也；伐遠功成者以之，不亦可勞乎？此勞還師之詩，若謂我將帥之于征也，昔固覩雨雪而懷憂矣，今其歸也，不有感時而可樂者耶？是故青陽應候，暄和而舒長，維天時則春矣；卉木含滋，蒙密而茂盛，觀物態則變矣。倉庚之聲，清和圓轉，得氣何先也！采蘩之女，往來衆多，治蠶何蚤也！斯時也，輳門繫當訊之渠魁，行間從被獲之群醜，却狄之功成矣。即長途而悠悠于邁，指王國而𩤸𩤸啓行，全歸之樂遂矣。是果誰之功哉？乃我南仲，才足以禦侮，威望
translation_en:
…Taking prisoners for questioning and capturing the enemy host, they return home beneath their banners. Glorious is Nan Zhong: the Xianyun have been subdued.

Wang Jiayan.

Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔He conveys the Zhou dynasty’s intention in honoring its troops.〕
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: 〔The writing is vigorous and spirited, neither dry nor superficial; it merits selection.〕
Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: 〔The diction and tone are classical and elegant, achieving a gentle and generous manner.〕
Examiner Wang, School Director, comments: 〔Closely structured and refined.〕
Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: 〔It portrays the atmosphere of a flourishing age.〕

The poet recounts the joy of the great general’s returning army and reveals the greatness of his achievement. To ride forth [?] and sound the song of victory is indeed joyful. When those who have campaigned afar and achieved success do so, should they not also be honored? This poem honoring the returning troops seems to say: when our commanders went on campaign, they saw the falling snow and felt anxious. Now that they return, does the season not stir feelings that bring them joy?

Thus spring’s warmth arrives in its season, mild and expansive: in the course of heaven, spring has come. Plants and trees are imbued with moisture, dense and luxuriant: the appearance of things has changed. The orioles’ calls are clear, harmonious, and melodious—how early they respond to the season’s vital force! Women gathering white southernwood come and go in numbers—how early they tend their silkworms!

At this time, the ringleaders awaiting interrogation are bound at the gate [?], and the captured enemy host follows among the ranks: the work of repelling the Di is accomplished. They take the long road and travel steadily onward; setting their course toward the royal capital, they begin their march in orderly array [?]. The joy of returning with their forces intact is fulfilled.

Whose achievement is this, indeed? It is that of our Nan Zhong, whose ability suffices to ward off aggression, and whose prestige …

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
素著于華夷謀足以折衝聲名丕顯于遐邇其
于玁狁也據形勝以竣大防潛消其桀驁之氣
無復猾夏之敢圖孔棘之患維其紓矣嚴城守
以建長策陰折其覬覦之心無復王誅之敢干
孔熾之難其免矣夫謂之曰于夷信乎不戰屈
人而外患寧矣雖然來則禦禦之去則勿追先王
制御夷狄之常道也而或者猶有說焉曰其本
不在威強而在德業其備不在邊鄙而在朝廷
其具不在兵食而在紀綱噫此探本之論禦戎
之方掌邦政者所宜知也雖然豈獨司馬而已
哉
王曰然
賦政于外四方爰發

同考試官教諭趙　批〔講賦政爰發之意明盡〕
同考試官教諭馬　批〔詞語莊重宜錄以式多士〕
考試官學正王　批〔能道中興復古氣象〕
考試官教授許　批〔文有思致〕
punctuated:
素著于華夷，謀足以折衝，聲名丕顯于遐邇。其于玁狁也，據形勝以竣大防，潛消其桀驁之氣，無復猾夏之敢圖，孔棘之患維其紓矣；嚴城守以建長策，陰折其覬覦之心，無復王誅之敢干，孔熾之難其免矣。夫謂之曰「于夷」，信乎不戰屈人而外患寧矣。雖然，來則禦禦之，去則勿追，先王制御夷狄之常道也。而或者猶有說焉，曰：「其本不在威強而在德業，其備不在邊鄙而在朝廷，其具不在兵食而在紀綱。」噫！此探本之論、禦戎之方，掌邦政者所宜知也。雖然，豈獨司馬而已哉！
王曰：「然。」
賦政于外，四方爰發。

translation_en:
…his prestige had long been established among both the Chinese and the foreign peoples; his strategic ability sufficed to turn back hostile forces, and his reputation shone far and near. In dealing with the Xianyun, he occupied strategically advantageous terrain to complete the great defenses, quietly dissipating their rebellious spirit, so that they no longer dared contemplate disturbing the Chinese realm: the grievously urgent danger was thus relieved. He strengthened the defense of the cities to establish a lasting strategy, secretly breaking their covetous ambitions, so that they no longer dared incur royal punishment: the fiercely raging calamity was thus averted. Calling this “pacification” is indeed justified: he subdued others without fighting, and external troubles were stilled. Nevertheless, to repel them when they come [?] and refrain from pursuing them when they withdraw was the constant way by which the former kings controlled foreign peoples. Yet some offer a further argument: “Its foundation lies not in military might but in moral achievement; its preparedness lies not on the frontiers but at court; its instruments lie not in troops and provisions but in the governing order.” Ah! This argument that probes the root, this method of resisting foreign incursions, is something those who administer the state ought to understand. Yet does it concern the Minister of War alone?
The king said, “So it is.”
“Disseminate governance abroad, and the four quarters will respond.”
Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition is classically sound [?] and conveys the meaning of ordering affairs.〕
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning of “disseminating governance” and “responding” is explained clearly and fully.〕
Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: 〔The language is dignified; this should be included as a model for the many candidates.〕
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔It succeeds in expressing the spirit of dynastic revival and restoration of ancient practices.〕
Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: 〔The composition shows thoughtful refinement.〕

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
宣化於天下而皆得其應王命大臣之職也夫
經營職之重者也化宣于外而丕應焉職斯盡
矣王命大臣而以是期之宜哉昔宣王命仲山
甫城齊而尹吉甫作詩以送之此則述王命以
經營之職若謂夷厲以來不用其良四國之無
政久矣甫其循行方國求旬求宣渙中興之命
令共和當國未究其施人心之望治切矣甫其
遍歷侯邦咨諏咨詢振維新之事功順天下更
失理所以謀之廟堂者其即敷之下國乎喻德
===
教舉遺士所以圖之密勿者其即施之有政乎
是政也上賦之下未有以應之猶賦之未至也
其感之必發渙汗之下凡仰中興之治者咸興
媚順之心導之即從振刷之餘凡沐維新之化
者同起來歸之念天下順而人心服也失理更
而治道隆也四海雖遠殆有翕然其向風者矣
德教喻而士民慶也遺士舉而賢才進也天下
雖大殆有黴然其順治者矣否則如政之布何
哉吁此見山甫德之全而任之重也圖宜吉甫
punctuated: 宣化於天下而皆得其應，王命大臣之職也。夫經營，職之重者也。化宣于外而丕應焉，職斯盡矣。王命大臣而以是期之，宜哉！昔宣王命仲山甫城齊，而尹吉甫作詩以送之。此則述王命以經營之職，若謂夷厲以來，不用其良，四國之無政久矣。甫其循行方國，求旬求宣，渙中興之命令。共和當國，未究其施，人心之望治切矣。甫其遍歷侯邦，咨諏咨詢，振維新之事功。順天下，更失理，所以謀之廟堂者，其即敷之下國乎？喻德教，舉遺士，所以圖之密勿者，其即施之有政乎？是政也，上賦之，下未有以應之，猶賦之未至也。其感之必發，渙汗之下，凡仰中興之治者，咸興媚順之心；導之即從，振刷之餘，凡沐維新之化者，同起來歸之念。天下順而人心服也，失理更而治道隆也。四海雖遠，殆有翕然其向風者矣。德教喻而士民慶也，遺士舉而賢才進也。天下雖大，殆有黴然其順治者矣。否則如政之布何哉？吁！此見山甫德之全而任之重也。圖宜吉甫
translation_en:
To spread transforming influence throughout the realm and obtain a response everywhere: this is the duty the king assigns to his great ministers. The ordering of affairs is a weighty responsibility. When transforming influence spreads abroad and meets with a great response, that duty is fulfilled. How fitting that the king should appoint great ministers with this expectation!

Formerly, King Xuan commanded Zhong Shanfu to fortify Qi, and Yin Jifu composed a poem to see him off. This passage recounts the royal command entrusting him with the ordering of affairs, as though saying: “Since the reigns of Kings Yi and Li, worthy men have not been employed, and the lands of the four quarters have long lacked proper government. You, Shanfu, should travel through the regional states, attending to their affairs and spreading royal influence, promulgating the commands of the restoration. During the Gonghe regency, their implementation was not carried through, and the people keenly long for good government. You, Shanfu, should visit all the domains of the regional lords, seeking advice and making inquiries, and bring renewed vigor to the work of renovation. Bring order to the realm and correct misgovernment: should not what has been planned at court now be extended to the states below? Make moral instruction understood and raise overlooked scholars to office: should not what has been devised through diligent deliberation now be put into governmental practice?”

If these measures are assigned from above but meet with no response below, it is as though their assignment has not fully reached its destination. Their influence must call forth a response. Once royal commands issue forth, like sweat that cannot be recalled, all who look up to the government of the restoration will cherish willing obedience. Once guided, they will follow: after this reinvigoration, all who receive the transforming influence of renewal will share the desire to come and give their allegiance. The realm will be brought into order, and the people's hearts will submit; misgovernment will be corrected, and the way of good government will flourish. Though the lands within the Four Seas are distant, surely they will turn as one toward this influence. When moral instruction is understood, scholars and common people will rejoice; when overlooked scholars are raised to office, worthy talent will advance. Vast though the realm is, surely its people will submit to good government in accord [?]. Otherwise, what purpose would the promulgation of these measures serve?

Ah! Here we see the completeness of Shanfu's virtue and the weight of his responsibilities. It was therefore fitting [?] that Jifu…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
述之以慰城齊之心哉抑觀聖主得賢臣而弘
功業在古然矣宣王有吉甫召虎山甫數臣用
以攘狄平夷城齊卒有成功固可嘉已雖然城
道無成有終誦烝民諸詩而益見周家中興之
盛云
春秋
冬楚人伐黃〔僖公十有一年〕
張應
同考試官學正韓　批〔此題重在責齊作者類以〕
〔憫黃並講殊失本旨是篇深得傳意錄之〕
===
考試官學正王　批〔得聖人罪齊意〕
考試官教授許　批〔謹嚴〕
春秋特紀遠國之被兵所以深罪伯主之失職
此齊桓始結黃而終棄之春秋特書以致意宜
哉且楚何為而伐黃也以黃職貢之不至也職
貢不至而楚伐之宜罪之不在齊也春秋特書
伐而異於滅弦滅溫以罪桓公者何居誠以事
莫難於謀始尤莫難於慮終齊得黃而與之盟
punctuated:
述之以慰城齊之心哉！抑觀聖主得賢臣而弘功業，在古然矣。宣王有吉甫、召虎、山甫數臣，用以攘狄、平夷、城齊，卒有成功，固可嘉已。雖然，城道無成有終，誦《烝民》諸詩，而益見周家中興之盛云。
春秋
冬，楚人伐黃。〔僖公十有一年〕
張應
同考試官學正韓　批〔此題重在責齊，作者類以〕〔憫黃並講，殊失本旨。是篇深得傳意，錄之。〕
考試官學正王　批〔得聖人罪齊意。〕
考試官教授許　批〔謹嚴。〕
《春秋》特紀遠國之被兵，所以深罪伯主之失職。此齊桓始結黃而終棄之，《春秋》特書以致意，宜哉！且楚何為而伐黃也？以黃職貢之不至也。職貢不至而楚伐之，宜罪之不在齊也。《春秋》特書伐，而異於滅弦、滅溫，以罪桓公者，何居？誠以事莫難於謀始，尤莫難於慮終。齊得黃而與之盟
translation_en:
…recount it to console the heart of the man who fortified Qi! Moreover, that a sage ruler obtains worthy ministers and thereby enlarges his achievements was already true in antiquity. King Xuan had such ministers as Jifu, Shao Hu, and Shanfu, whom he employed to repel the Di, pacify the Yi, and fortify Qi. That they ultimately succeeded is certainly praiseworthy. Nevertheless, the way of fortification [?] claims no achievement of its own but brings matters to completion. Reading “The Multitudes of the People” (Zheng min) and the other poems, one sees still more clearly the splendor of the Zhou house’s resurgence.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In winter, men of Chu attacked Huang.” 〔The eleventh year of Duke Xi.〕

Zhang Ying

Comment by Associate Examiner Han, School Instructor: 〔The emphasis of this topic lies in censuring Qi. Writers generally〕〔discuss compassion for Huang alongside it, seriously missing the essential point. This essay thoroughly grasps the commentary’s meaning and has therefore been selected.〕

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: 〔Grasps the Sage’s intention to condemn Qi.〕

Comment by Examiner Xu, Professor: 〔Careful and rigorous.〕

The Spring and Autumn Annals specifically records a distant state’s suffering an attack in order to condemn severely the hegemon’s failure in his duties. Here, Duke Huan of Qi first allied himself with Huang but ultimately abandoned it. How fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals should make a special record of this to convey its meaning! Now, why did Chu attack Huang? Because Huang’s prescribed tribute had not arrived. If Chu attacked because the prescribed tribute had not arrived, surely the blame should not lie with Qi. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically write “attacked,” distinguishing this from the destruction of Xian and the destruction of Wen, in order to condemn Duke Huan? It is truly because, in undertaking affairs, nothing is harder than planning the beginning, and harder still is considering the outcome. Qi won Huang over and entered into a covenant with it…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
則足以成伯業桓之始謀也楚伐黃而不能救
則無以宗諸侯仲之終慮也使桓不以已之謀
為可恃而以仲之慮為可聽雖無當時服黃之
功亦未必有今日滅黃之慘夫何違敬仲之嘉
言結貫澤之新好齊喜於得黃而制楚之謀遂
決楚憾於附齊而取黃之心已萌曾幾何時楚
暴遂肆兵傳城下已歷三時之久告至臨菑竟
無一騎之援殊不思救患分災同盟事也攘夷
安夏伯主職也黃既有剝床近膚之憂齊遂當
===
為被髮纓冠之舉顧乃袖手旁觀寒貫澤之盟
而罔恤忍心坐視棄禮義之君而莫圖借曰道
遠行艱莫能救也然黃昔以遠而至中國今柰
何以為遠而弗往救乎借曰小國不恭自取禍
也然黃以恃齊而不歸楚貢今柰何使皭人卑
心而弗動念乎卒之楚氛益惡黃社遂墟回視
前日即華之行適為今日滅亡之地桓之罪其
可追哉故春秋於滅弦滅温皆不書伐者以其
非同盟也特書伐於滅黃之上者罪桓公既與
punctuated: 則足以成伯業，桓之始謀也；楚伐黃而不能救，則無以宗諸侯，仲之終慮也。使桓不以已之謀為可恃，而以仲之慮為可聽，雖無當時服黃之功，亦未必有今日滅黃之慘。夫何違敬仲之嘉言，結貫澤之新好？齊喜於得黃，而制楚之謀遂決；楚憾於附齊，而取黃之心已萌。曾幾何時，楚暴遂肆，兵傳城下，已歷三時之久；告至臨菑，竟無一騎之援。殊不思救患分災，同盟事也；攘夷安夏，伯主職也。黃既有剝床近膚之憂，齊遂當為被髮纓冠之舉。顧乃袖手旁觀，寒貫澤之盟而罔恤；忍心坐視，棄禮義之君而莫圖。借曰道遠行艱，莫能救也，然黃昔以遠而至中國，今柰何以為遠而弗往救乎？借曰小國不恭，自取禍也，然黃以恃齊而不歸楚貢，今柰何使皭人卑心而弗動念乎？卒之楚氛益惡，黃社遂墟。回視前日即華之行，適為今日滅亡之地。桓之罪，其可追哉！故《春秋》於滅弦、滅温皆不書伐者，以其非同盟也；特書伐於滅黃之上者，罪桓公既與
translation_en:
…would suffice to establish his hegemony: this was Duke Huan’s initial calculation. If Chu attacked Huang and he could not rescue it, he would have no means of commanding the allegiance of the regional lords: this was Guan Zhong’s concern about the eventual outcome. Had Duke Huan not considered his own calculations dependable, but regarded Guan Zhong’s concerns as worth heeding, then, even without the achievement of winning Huang’s submission at that time, there might never have been the tragedy of Huang’s destruction today. Why, then, did he disregard Jingzhong’s sound advice and establish new amity at Guanze? Qi rejoiced at gaining Huang, and its plan to restrain Chu was thus settled; Chu resented Huang’s attachment to Qi, and already conceived the desire to seize it. Before long, Chu unleashed its violence. Its troops reached the city walls [?], and three seasons had already passed. Appeals reached Linzi, yet not a single mounted soldier came to its aid.

He utterly failed to consider that rescuing those in distress and sharing the burden of calamity are the duties of allies, and that repelling the barbarians and securing the Chinese states are the responsibilities of a hegemon. With Huang already facing peril as immediate as a bed being stripped away almost to the skin, Qi should have rushed to act, with hair unbound and cap hastily tied on. Instead, he stood by with folded arms, letting the covenant of Guanze grow cold without concern; hardening his heart, he watched idly, abandoning a ruler who observed ritual propriety and righteousness, without devising any plan. Suppose he pleaded that the road was long and travel difficult, so that rescue was impossible. Yet Huang had formerly come to the central states from afar; how could he now use its remoteness as a reason not to go to its rescue? Suppose he pleaded that this small state had been disrespectful and brought disaster upon itself. Yet it was because Huang relied on Qi that it withheld tribute from Chu. How could he now make an upright man humble himself [?], without giving the matter a thought?

In the end, Chu’s menace grew ever more severe, and Huang’s altars of soil became ruins. Looking back, Huang’s earlier act of attaching itself to the Chinese states had become the very ground of its destruction today. Could Duke Huan’s guilt be pursued back to its source! Thus, when recording the destruction of Xian and Wen, the Spring and Autumn Annals does not record an attack, because they were not members of the same alliance. Its particular recording of an attack before Huang’s destruction condemns Duke Huan for having already participated in…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
會盟而又不能救也聖筆之嚴有如是哉抑又
論之遠國慕義背夷即華正也仲欲拒之非矣
仲之意特料桓公無以善其後故也伯盍戒於
舜曰無怠無荒四夷來王仲不能示其君以怠
荒之戒而預憂其棄黃亦非忠臣事君之道也
雖然仲不死則黃未必滅若仲者又豈可以盡
非哉
夏六月乙卯晉荀林父帥師及楚子戰于
邲晉師敗績〔宣公十有二年〕晉欒書帥師救
===
鄭〔成公六年〕
張東銘
同考試官學正韓 批〔林父欒書用兵得失胡傳〕
〔甚明作者往往遺之此作會傳成文故錄以式〕
考試官學正王 批〔有斷制〕
考試官教授許 批〔聖經予奪意如此〕
交兵而失專制之義者可責恤患而得專制之
義者可予此林父之戰楚敗績欒書之救鄭還
師其得失俱不容掩於書法間矣在昔宣公中
punctuated:
會盟而又不能救也。聖筆之嚴，有如是哉！抑又論之，遠國慕義，背夷即華，正也；仲欲拒之，非矣。仲之意，特料桓公無以善其後故也。伯盍戒於舜曰：「無怠無荒，四夷來王。」仲不能示其君以怠荒之戒，而預憂其棄黃，亦非忠臣事君之道也。雖然，仲不死，則黃未必滅。若仲者，又豈可以盡非哉？
夏六月乙卯，晉荀林父帥師及楚子戰于邲，晉師敗績。〔宣公十有二年〕晉欒書帥師救鄭。〔成公六年〕
張東銘
同考試官學正韓批〔林父欒書用兵得失，胡傳〕〔甚明。作者往往遺之，此作會傳成文，故錄以式。〕
考試官學正王批〔有斷制。〕
考試官教授許批〔聖經予奪意如此。〕
交兵而失專制之義者，可責；恤患而得專制之義者，可予。此林父之戰楚敗績，欒書之救鄭還師，其得失俱不容掩於書法間矣。在昔宣公中
translation_en:
…had joined in a covenant with them, yet could not rescue them. Such is the severity of the Sage’s brush! To consider the matter further: for a distant state to admire righteousness, turn away from the barbarians, and join the Chinese states was right; for Zhong (Guan Zhong) to wish to reject it was wrong. Zhong’s intention arose solely from his judgment that Duke Huan would be unable to bring the matter to a satisfactory conclusion. Bo He [?] admonished Shun, saying: “Be neither idle nor negligent, and the barbarians of the four quarters will come to acknowledge your kingship.” Zhong failed to impress upon his ruler this warning against idleness and negligence, instead worrying beforehand that he would abandon Huang. This, too, was not the way a loyal minister should serve his ruler. Even so, had Zhong not died, Huang might not have been destroyed. How, then, could a man like Zhong be condemned in every respect?
