嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
則足以成伯業桓之始謀也楚伐黃而不能救
則無以宗諸侯仲之終慮也使桓不以已之謀
為可恃而以仲之慮為可聽雖無當時服黃之
功亦未必有今日滅黃之慘夫何違敬仲之嘉
言結貫澤之新好齊喜於得黃而制楚之謀遂
決楚憾於附齊而取黃之心已萌曾幾何時楚
暴遂肆兵傳城下已歷三時之久告至臨菑竟
無一騎之援殊不思救患分災同盟事也攘夷
安夏伯主職也黃既有剝床近膚之憂齊遂當
===
為被髮纓冠之舉顧乃袖手旁觀寒貫澤之盟
而罔恤忍心坐視棄禮義之君而莫圖借曰道
遠行艱莫能救也然黃昔以遠而至中國今柰
何以為遠而弗往救乎借曰小國不恭自取禍
也然黃以恃齊而不歸楚貢今柰何使罹人井
心而弗動念乎卒之楚氛益惡黃社遂墟回視
前日即華之行適為今日滅亡之地桓之罪其
可逭哉故春秋於滅弦滅溫皆不書伐者以其
非同盟也特書伐於滅黃之上者罪桓公既與
punctuated: 則足以成伯業，桓之始謀也；楚伐黃而不能救，則無以宗諸侯，仲之終慮也。使桓不以已之謀為可恃，而以仲之慮為可聽，雖無當時服黃之功，亦未必有今日滅黃之慘。夫何違敬仲之嘉言，結貫澤之新好？齊喜於得黃，而制楚之謀遂決；楚憾於附齊，而取黃之心已萌。曾幾何時，楚暴遂肆，兵傳城下，已歷三時之久；告至臨菑，竟無一騎之援。殊不思救患分災，同盟事也；攘夷安夏，伯主職也。黃既有剝床近膚之憂，齊遂當為被髮纓冠之舉。顧乃袖手旁觀，寒貫澤之盟而罔恤；忍心坐視，棄禮義之君而莫圖。借曰道遠行艱，莫能救也，然黃昔以遠而至中國，今柰何以為遠而弗往救乎？借曰小國不恭，自取禍也，然黃以恃齊而不歸楚貢，今柰何使罹人井心而弗動念乎？卒之楚氛益惡，黃社遂墟。回視前日即華之行，適為今日滅亡之地。桓之罪，其可逭哉？故春秋於滅弦、滅溫皆不書伐者，以其非同盟也；特書伐於滅黃之上者，罪桓公既與
translation_en: …would thus suffice to establish hegemony: this was Huan’s initial plan. But if Chu attacked Huang and he could not rescue it, he would have no means of commanding the allegiance of the feudal lords: this was Zhong’s concern about the eventual outcome. Had Duke Huan regarded his own plan as less dependable and Zhong’s concerns as worthy of a hearing, then, even without the achievement of bringing Huang into submission at that time, there need not have been the tragedy of Huang’s destruction today. Why, then, did he disregard the excellent words of Jingzhong (Guan Zhong) and establish new friendly relations at Guanze? Qi rejoiced at gaining Huang, and its plan to restrain Chu was settled; Chu resented Huang’s attachment to Qi, and the intention to seize Huang had already taken root. Before long, Chu unleashed its violence. Its troops reached the city walls, and three seasons had already elapsed; appeals reached Linzi, yet not a single horseman came to help. Huan utterly failed to consider that rescuing one another from trouble and sharing the burden of calamity are the duties of allies, and that repelling the non-Chinese peoples and securing the Chinese states are the responsibilities of a hegemon. Since Huang faced danger like a bed being stripped away until the destruction approached the sleeper’s skin, Qi should have rushed to its aid with hair unbound and cap hastily tied on. Instead, Huan stood by with folded arms, letting the covenant of Guanze grow cold without concern; hardening his heart, he watched idly, abandoning a ruler who observed ritual and righteousness without devising any remedy. Suppose he said that the road was long and travel difficult, making rescue impossible: Huang had formerly come to the central states despite its distance, so how could he now plead that distance as a reason not to go to its aid? Suppose he said that a small state had been disrespectful and brought disaster upon itself: Huang had withheld tribute from Chu because it relied upon Qi, so how could he let it fall into a pit of calamity [?] without giving it a thought? In the end, Chu’s menace grew still worse, and Huang’s altars of state became ruins. Looking back, Huang’s earlier act of attaching itself to the Chinese states had become the very basis of its destruction today. Could Huan escape blame for this? Thus, in recording the destruction of Xian and Wen, the Spring and Autumn Annals does not mention an attack, because they were not members of the alliance. Its particular mention of an attack before recording Huang’s destruction condemns Duke Huan for having already joined with…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
年楚伐鄭而晉救之于邲交綏晉以敗告則辱
可知矣春秋既不以救鄭書而又以林父主是
戰者豈不曰無故伐鄭楚則有罪也亦既退師
與鄭平矣使為林父計者無及於鄭全師而還
猶之可也夫何輕與楚戰喪師辱國誰之責乎
借曰先縠欲戰不得已而從之耳殊不知將在
軍君令有所不受况當是時不欲劓民者三帥
也違命濟師特先縠一中軍佐而已不能執專
制之權而以軍法行之乃畏失屬亡師之罪從
===
韓獻子分惡之言忿不思難遂與楚戰則是亟
戰殘民進退不由於已者也林父之罪重矣春
秋不以救許晉而及在林父其責之也蓋如此
成公初年楚又伐鄭而晉救之桑隧一遇晉以
師還則功無可錄矣春秋乃以救許晉而深善
欒書之不戰者豈不曰乘喪伐鄭楚固不能無
罪也然既釋鄭以還師矣使為欒書計者致怒
于楚决意進師亦何取哉所幸還師避敵保國
惜民何功如之借曰軍帥欲戰者八人盡從衆
punctuated:
年，楚伐鄭，而晉救之，于邲交綏，晉以敗告，則辱可知矣。《春秋》既不以救鄭書，而又以林父主是戰者，豈不曰：無故伐鄭，楚則有罪也；亦既退師，與鄭平矣。使為林父計者，無及於鄭，全師而還，猶之可也。夫何輕與楚戰，喪師辱國，誰之責乎？借曰：「先縠欲戰，不得已而從之耳。」殊不知將在軍，君令有所不受。况當是時，不欲劓民者三帥也；違命濟師，特先縠一中軍佐而已。不能執專制之權，而以軍法行之，乃畏失屬亡師之罪，從韓獻子分惡之言，忿不思難，遂與楚戰，則是亟戰殘民，進退不由於已者也。林父之罪重矣！《春秋》不以救許晉，而及在林父，其責之也蓋如此。

成公初年，楚又伐鄭，而晉救之，桑隧一遇，晉以師還，則功無可錄矣。《春秋》乃以救許晉，而深善欒書之不戰者，豈不曰：乘喪伐鄭，楚固不能無罪也；然既釋鄭以還師矣。使為欒書計者，致怒于楚，决意進師，亦何取哉？所幸還師避敵，保國惜民，何功如之？借曰：「軍帥欲戰者八人，盡從衆
translation_en:
…in that year, Chu attacked Zheng, and Jin came to its rescue. They met in battle at Bi, and Jin reported its defeat: its humiliation is plain. The Spring and Autumn Annals neither records this as a rescue of Zheng nor leaves any doubt that Linfu was responsible for the battle. Is its meaning not this? Chu was culpable for attacking Zheng without cause, but it had already withdrawn its army and made peace with Zheng. Had one been advising Linfu, it would still have been acceptable to return with his army intact without reaching Zheng. Why, then, did he rashly fight Chu, losing his army and humiliating his state? Whose responsibility was this? Suppose one argues: “Xian Hu wanted to fight; Linfu had no choice but to follow him.” This entirely overlooks the principle that a general in the field may refuse even his ruler’s commands. Moreover, at that time three commanders wished to avoid mutilating the people, while the only man who disobeyed orders and took his troops across the river was Xian Hu, the assistant commander of the central army. Linfu failed to exercise his authority to decide independently and enforce military law against him. Instead, fearing that he would be charged with losing control of a subordinate and losing an army, he followed Han Xianzi’s advice to share the blame. In anger, without considering the dangers, he proceeded to fight Chu. Thus he rushed into battle and injured the people, unable to determine his own advance or retreat. Grave indeed was Linfu’s guilt! The Spring and Autumn Annals denies Jin credit for a rescue and attributes the engagement to Linfu: such, presumably, is the grounds for its censure.

In the first year of Duke Cheng, Chu again attacked Zheng, and Jin came to its rescue. After an encounter at Sangsui, Jin brought its army home; apparently there was no achievement worth recording. Yet the Spring and Autumn Annals credits Jin with a rescue and warmly approves Luan Shu’s refusal to fight. Is its meaning not this? Chu certainly could not escape blame for attacking Zheng during its mourning, but it had already left Zheng alone and withdrawn its army. Had one been advising Luan Shu, what benefit would there have been in directing his anger against Chu and resolving to advance? Fortunately, he withdrew his army and avoided the enemy, protecting his state and sparing the people. What achievement could equal this? Suppose one argues: “Eight of the army’s commanders wanted to fight; to follow the majority in everything…”

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
以濟事乎殊不思閫以外將軍制之況當是時
不欲亟戰者三帥也而欲阻兵以逞特同括輩
六軍之屬而巳乃能持專制之柄而以軍法斷
之不還戮以慭楚遂退師以全民我則未病鄭
亦無虞則是以不戰為功進退必由於巳者也
欒書之功偉矣春秋以救許晉而深善其不戰
其予之也蓋如此噫同一救鄭也林父將則辱
國欒書將則全民人君用人之際可不慎哉大
抵天下有大道理名與分而巳矣先穀同括六
===
軍之佐屬也乃不奉主帥之命而輒欲行巳之
私是懵於道理不知名分為何物也卒之先穀
不得其死同括亦以譖而就戮雖能逃一時之
斧鉞而終無以免後日之禍患則亦其無上之
心有以取之耳噫以此垂訓後世猶有慢軍令
而舍水上山如馬謖違節制而深入不巳如任
福者自取夷滅亦獨何心哉
禮記
天子以德為車以樂為御諸侯以禮相與
punctuated:
以濟事乎？殊不思閫以外，將軍制之。況當是時，不欲亟戰者三帥也，而欲阻兵以逞，特同括輩六軍之屬而巳。乃能持專制之柄，而以軍法斷之，不還戮以慭楚，遂退師以全民。我則未病，鄭亦無虞，則是以不戰為功，進退必由於巳者也。欒書之功偉矣！春秋以救許晉，而深善其不戰，其予之也蓋如此。噫！同一救鄭也，林父將則辱國，欒書將則全民，人君用人之際，可不慎哉？大抵天下有大道理，名與分而巳矣。先穀、同括，六軍之佐屬也，乃不奉主帥之命，而輒欲行巳之私，是懵於道理，不知名分為何物也。卒之先穀不得其死，同括亦以譖而就戮。雖能逃一時之斧鉞，而終無以免後日之禍患，則亦其無上之心有以取之耳。噫！以此垂訓後世，猶有慢軍令而舍水上山如馬謖、違節制而深入不巳如任福者，自取夷滅，亦獨何心哉？

禮記

天子以德為車，以樂為御，諸侯以禮相與。
translation_en:
…to accomplish the undertaking? This utterly overlooks the principle that beyond the palace threshold, the general exercises command. Moreover, at that time the three commanders did not wish to rush into battle; those who wished to rely on armed force to satisfy their ambitions were merely Tong and Kuo and their fellows, subordinate officers of the six armies. Yet Luan Shu was able to exercise his independent authority and decide the matter according to military law. He did not turn back to inflict slaughter and thereby distress Chu [?], but withdrew his army to preserve the people. Our side suffered no harm, and Zheng likewise faced no danger. Thus he achieved merit by not fighting, retaining control over both advance and retreat. Great indeed was Luan Shu’s achievement! The Spring and Autumn Annals credits Jin with coming to the rescue and warmly commends his refusal to fight: such was its approbation of him. Alas! Both expeditions were undertaken to rescue Zheng, yet with Lin Fu in command the state was disgraced, while with Luan Shu in command the people were preserved. Can a ruler afford to be careless when appointing men?

Broadly speaking, the great principles governing the world amount simply to proper status and allotted duty. Xian Gu [?], Tong, and Kuo were subordinate officers of the six armies, yet they refused to obey the commander’s orders and sought instead to pursue their private wishes. This shows that they were blind to principle and did not know what proper status and duty meant. In the end, Xian Gu met an untimely death, and Tong and Kuo were also executed following slanderous accusations. Although they could escape the executioner’s axe for a time, they ultimately could not avoid later calamity. It was their disposition to acknowledge no superior that brought this upon them. Alas! Despite this lesson handed down to later generations, there were still men such as Ma Su, who disregarded military orders and abandoned the water to ascend a mountain, and Ren Fu, who violated the commander’s directives and kept advancing deep into enemy territory. What could have possessed them to bring destruction upon themselves?

Book of Rites

The Son of Heaven takes virtue as his carriage and music as his charioteer; the feudal lords associate with one another through ritual propriety…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
大夫以法相序士以信相考百姓以睦相
守天下之肥也
李檀
同考試官教諭張　批〔此題作者多於天下肥處　不能形容此作發明殆盡宜錄出以式學者〕
考試官學正王　批〔簡明可取〕
考試官教授許　批〔能發揮大順意〕
舉天下之人盡其道見天下之治極其充焉甚
矣治以大順為至也人人盡其道而天下平矣
===
非聖王孰能與於此禮運言修道之教及此謂
夫聖王之治達於順猶人之食期於肥然治之
所謂肥焉者豈特由身而家而國然哉推之天
下亦有可見者矣是故天子者德以出治德匪
車也仁義之道利攸往矣其以德為車乎樂以
導和樂匪御也鑾和之聲行斯中矣其以樂為
御乎諸侯相與朝聘以時也大小竭藩屏之誠
大夫相序等威已辨也上下安靖共之位篤信
之道久要不忘者士之行也和睦之風循為爾
punctuated:
大夫以法相序，士以信相考，百姓以睦相守，天下之肥也。

李檀

同考試官教諭張　批〔此題作者多於天下肥處不能形容，此作發明殆盡，宜錄出以式學者。〕
考試官學正王　批〔簡明可取。〕
考試官教授許　批〔能發揮大順意。〕

舉天下之人盡其道，見天下之治極其充焉。甚矣，治以大順為至也！人人盡其道，而天下平矣。非聖王，孰能與於此？禮運言修道之教，及此謂夫聖王之治達於順，猶人之食期於肥然。治之所謂肥焉者，豈特由身而家而國然哉？推之天下，亦有可見者矣。是故天子者，德以出治。德匪車也，仁義之道，利攸往矣，其以德為車乎？樂以導和。樂匪御也，鑾和之聲，行斯中矣，其以樂為御乎？諸侯相與，朝聘以時也，大小竭藩屏之誠；大夫相序，等威已辨也，上下安靖共之位。篤信之道，久要不忘者，士之行也；和睦之風，循為爾
translation_en:
… The great officers order their relations by established rules; the shi assess one another by trustworthiness; the common people sustain one another through concord: this is the flourishing of All-under-Heaven.

Li Tan 李檀

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Most writers addressing this topic cannot adequately describe the flourishing of All-under-Heaven. This essay elucidates it almost exhaustively and should be recorded as a model for students.〕
Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: 〔Concise and clear; worthy of acceptance.〕
Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: 〔It succeeds in developing the meaning of the Great Accord.〕

When all the people of All-under-Heaven fulfill their proper way, we see its government attain the utmost fullness. How truly the highest attainment of government lies in the Great Accord! When everyone fulfills their proper way, All-under-Heaven is at peace. Who but a sage king could attain this? The “Evolution of Rites” chapter discusses the teaching that cultivates the Way. At this point it means that the sage king’s government attains accord, just as a person eats with the aim of becoming well nourished. Yet can what is called “flourishing” in government apply only to the progression from oneself to one’s household and then one’s state? Extended to All-under-Heaven, it too has visible manifestations.

Thus the Son of Heaven brings forth good government through virtue. Virtue is no carriage, yet the way of benevolence and righteousness makes it beneficial to go forward: does he not take virtue as his carriage? Through music he guides people toward harmony. Music is no charioteer, yet to the sound of the carriage bells his movements attain due measure: does he not take music as his charioteer? The feudal lords maintain their relations through court audiences and diplomatic visits at the proper times; great and small alike devote themselves sincerely to serving as protective bulwarks. The great officers order their relations with distinctions of rank and authority clearly established; higher and lower alike rest secure in their positions of reverent service. Practicing steadfast trustworthiness and never forgetting old agreements is the conduct of the shi. As for the ethos of concord, whereby people follow your … [?]

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
德者民之尚也夫自天子以至於庶人天下之
人盡之矣一有乖焉不足以言肥也今也天子
和德於上矣臣民和德於下矣泰和之治達之
天下者無間也其充盛矣乎正朝廷以正百官
矣正百官以正萬民矣維新之化放之四海者
皆同也其至足矣乎是知人身之肥充於食天
下之肥則充於化也大順之道有如此豈非聖
學之極功哉抑是道也即易之化成書之於變
也豈易致哉必成己之功盡而後成物之效臻
===
其序有不可紊其功有不可闕者後世大學之
道不講舍其田而不治者多矣無惑乎大道之
日隱也喟然之嘆有由然矣
尊仁安義可謂用勞矣　孟淮
同考試官教諭張　批〔說尊安用勞字自是明暢錄之〕
考試官學正王　批〔詞意俱優〕
考試官教授許　批〔特取〕
punctuated:
德者，民之尚也。夫自天子以至於庶人，天下之人盡之矣。一有乖焉，不足以言肥也。今也，天子和德於上矣，臣民和德於下矣，泰和之治達之天下者無間也，其充盛矣乎！正朝廷以正百官矣，正百官以正萬民矣，維新之化放之四海者皆同也，其至足矣乎！是知人身之肥充於食，天下之肥則充於化也。大順之道有如此，豈非聖學之極功哉！抑是道也，即《易》之化成、《書》之於變也，豈易致哉！必成己之功盡，而後成物之效臻。其序有不可紊，其功有不可闕者。後世大學之道不講，舍其田而不治者多矣。無惑乎大道之日隱也，喟然之嘆有由然矣。
尊仁安義，可謂用勞矣。孟淮
同考試官教諭張，批〔說尊安用勞字自是明暢，錄之。〕
考試官學正王，批〔詞意俱優。〕
考試官教授許，批〔特取。〕
translation_en:
…virtue is what the common people esteem. From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, everyone under Heaven is included. If even one departs from this harmony, one cannot speak of flourishing. Now the Son of Heaven harmonizes virtue above, and officials and people harmonize virtue below. The rule of supreme harmony reaches throughout the realm without interruption: how abundant its flourishing! By rectifying the court, the hundred officials are rectified; by rectifying the hundred officials, the myriad people are rectified. The renewing transformation extends alike throughout the Four Seas: how complete its fulfillment! Thus we know that bodily fullness is sustained by food, while the flourishing of all under Heaven is sustained by moral transformation. Such is the Way of great accord. Is this not the ultimate achievement of sagely learning? This Way is precisely the “transformation and completion” of the Book of Changes and the “Oh, how they were transformed!” of the Book of Documents. How could it be attained easily? Only when the work of perfecting oneself is fully accomplished can the effects of perfecting others be realized. Its sequence must not be confused, and no part of its work may be omitted. In later ages, the Way of Great Learning has gone unstudied, and many abandon their own fields without cultivating them. No wonder the great Way becomes more obscure each day. There is good reason for that deep sigh.
“To honor benevolence and rest in righteousness may be called exerting oneself.” By Meng Huai.
Associate Examiner Zhang, an Instructor, comments: 〔The explanation of the words “honor,” “rest in,” and “exert oneself” is clear and fluent in its own right. Include it.〕
Examiner Wang, an Instructor, comments: 〔Both expression and meaning are excellent.〕
Examiner Xu, a Professor, comments: 〔Selected for special merit.〕

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
詳及物之勞著顯親之孝夫仁義盡於己而功
勞自及於物矣由是以成其親焉可謂中孝也
已曾子言孝有三此則舉中孝也意謂不容已
者人心之孝也不可踰者天下之分也所當自
盡者天下之道也所謂中孝用勞者果何如哉
彼為諸侯卿大夫士者知仁者天下之表所當
尊重而不可忽焉者則天爵是尊大其心以體
天下之物也良貴是崇弘其量以擴無我之公
也民胞物與之施一皆惻怛慈祥之愛矣育民
之道其盡矣乎義者天下之制所當安行而不
可悖焉者則正路是由裁制之而不過其則也
大道是行錯綜之而不爽其宜也執世宰物之
政一皆權衡矩度之施矣正民之道其盡矣乎
夫如是豈非用勞之孝哉蓋尊仁以育民而民
得其育焉則吾之勞著於民之育矣衆譽攸歸
之下人之敬於我者亦不棄其親也吾親之譽
隆謂非吾尊仁之所致邪安義以正民而民得
其正焉則吾之功著於民之正矣國人稱願之
punctuated: 詳及物之勞，著顯親之孝。夫仁義盡於己，而功勞自及於物矣。由是以成其親焉，可謂中孝也已。曾子言孝有三，此則舉中孝也。意謂不容已者，人心之孝也；不可踰者，天下之分也；所當自盡者，天下之道也。所謂中孝用勞者，果何如哉？彼為諸侯卿大夫士者，知仁者天下之表，所當尊重而不可忽焉者，則天爵是尊，大其心以體天下之物也；良貴是崇，弘其量以擴無我之公也。民胞物與之施，一皆惻怛慈祥之愛矣。育民之道，其盡矣乎！義者天下之制，所當安行而不可悖焉者，則正路是由，裁制之而不過其則也；大道是行，錯綜之而不爽其宜也。執世宰物之政，一皆權衡矩度之施矣。正民之道，其盡矣乎！夫如是，豈非用勞之孝哉？蓋尊仁以育民，而民得其育焉，則吾之勞著於民之育矣。衆譽攸歸之下，人之敬於我者，亦不棄其親也。吾親之譽隆，謂非吾尊仁之所致邪？安義以正民，而民得其正焉，則吾之功著於民之正矣。國人稱願之
translation_en:
Elaborate upon the service that benefits others, and make manifest the filial piety that brings honor to one’s parents. When one fully realizes benevolence and righteousness in oneself, one’s achievements and service naturally extend to others. By thereby bringing fulfillment to one’s parents, one may indeed attain the middle degree of filial piety. Zengzi spoke of three degrees of filial piety; here he addresses the middle degree. His meaning is that filial devotion in the human heart cannot be suppressed; the distinctions of station in the world cannot be overstepped; and the Way of the world requires one’s utmost exertion. What, then, is meant by rendering service as the middle degree of filial piety?

Those who are feudal lords, ministers, grand masters, or servicemen know that benevolence is the model for the world, which must be honored and never neglected. Thus they honor Heaven-conferred nobility, enlarging their hearts to embody all things under Heaven; they exalt their innate worth, broadening their capacity to extend the impartiality of selflessness. Their practice of treating the people as siblings and all things as companions consists entirely of compassionate, kindly love. Have they not fully realized the Way of nurturing the people? Righteousness is the governing standard for the world, which must be practiced with ease and never transgressed. Thus they follow the correct path, regulating affairs without exceeding its standards; they walk the great Way, handling the complexities of affairs without departing from what is fitting. Their government of the world and ordering of things consists entirely of applying proper weights, measures, and standards. Have they not fully realized the Way of rectifying the people?

Is this not filial piety expressed through service? By honoring benevolence one nurtures the people, and when the people receive that nurture, one’s service becomes manifest in their nourishment. As praise converges upon one from all quarters, those who respect one do not disregard one’s parents either. When one’s parents enjoy an exalted reputation, can one deny that this results from one’s honoring benevolence? By resting in righteousness one rectifies the people, and when the people attain rectitude, one’s achievement becomes manifest in their rectification. The praise and admiration [?] of the people of the state …

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
歸所以成其身者亦所以成其親也吾親之名
成謂非吾安義之所致邪所謂用勞之孝蓋如
此是知仁義者道之所當盡也用勞者孝之所
由成也中孝君子當知所事矣抑孝也者天之
經也地之義也拘於分固有三者之異要其心
之所以自盡者則一而已矣不然則菽水盡歡
者不足以為孝而歷山之耕何以稱其為大孝
終身之慕邪孟子曰孰不為事事親事之本也
孰不為守守身守之本也然則事親者必達於
所守之本而後可
===
第貳場
論
君子尊德性而道問學
吳三樂
同考試官教諭劉　批〔此題作者類皆掇拾浮詞〕
殊戾本旨惟此篇論尊德性道問學只以道一為主而
以學二要其同歸詞不繁而理獨到且通篇無一險怪
語非邃於理學者不能允宜高薦
punctuated:
歸，所以成其身者，亦所以成其親也。吾親之名成，謂非吾安義之所致邪？所謂用勞之孝，蓋如此。是知仁義者，道之所當盡也；用勞者，孝之所由成也。中孝君子，當知所事矣。抑孝也者，天之經也，地之義也。拘於分，固有三者之異；要其心之所以自盡者，則一而已矣。不然，則菽水盡歡者不足以為孝，而歷山之耕，何以稱其為大孝、終身之慕邪？孟子曰：「孰不為事？事親，事之本也。孰不為守？守身，守之本也。」然則事親者，必達於所守之本而後可。

第貳場
論
君子尊德性而道問學
吳三樂

同考試官教諭劉，批〔此題作者類皆掇拾浮詞〕殊戾本旨。惟此篇論尊德性、道問學，只以道一為主，而以學二要其同歸。詞不繁而理獨到，且通篇無一險怪語。非邃於理學者不能，允宜高薦。
translation_en:
…as such acclaim comes to him, what brings fulfillment to himself also brings fulfillment to his parents. When my parents’ good name is established, can this be anything but the result of my resting in righteousness? Such, indeed, is what is called filial piety through exertion. Thus we know that benevolence and righteousness are what one must fully realize in following the Way, and that exertion is how filial piety is accomplished. The gentleman practicing the intermediate degree of filial piety should know where to direct his service. Now filial piety is the constant principle of Heaven and the proper order of Earth. Insofar as it is bounded by one’s station, there are indeed differences among its three degrees; yet in the heart’s utmost devotion, they are one. Otherwise, those who bring their parents complete joy with only beans and water would not qualify as filial. And how could Shun’s plowing at Lishan be called great filial piety, an expression of his lifelong yearning for his parents? Mencius said: “What does not constitute service? Serving one’s parents is the foundation of service. What does not require safeguarding? Safeguarding oneself is the foundation of safeguarding.” Thus, to serve one’s parents, one must first comprehend the foundation of what one must safeguard.

Second Session
Discourse
“The gentleman honors his moral nature and pursues inquiry and learning.”
Wu Sanle

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔Most writers on this topic merely gather superficial phrases〕 and gravely depart from its essential meaning. This essay alone, in discussing honoring one’s moral nature and pursuing inquiry and learning, takes the unity of the Way as its governing principle and shows how the two approaches to learning converge upon the same end. Its language is concise, and its understanding of principle is exceptional. Moreover, throughout the essay there is not a single strained or eccentric expression. No one lacking profound mastery of the Learning of Principle could accomplish this. It truly deserves recommendation for a high place.

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭辛　批〔士子作此雖皆知為存心致知而不知其同歸於道以道一為說僅見此篇〕
考試官學正王　批〔作理學論如此篇者絶少〕
考試官教授許　批〔道一之說諸作皆不能到〕
學以盡道為極道一而學有二焉君子當要其
所歸也夫道者率性而已有二乎哉而學者之
法二之者何也不如是不足以盡道也道盡則
無二矣夫君子之學主於盡道而已道一而學
二以學之二而會道之一君子奚病於學哉尊
===
德性而道問學子思之言也尊德性學求於心
也道問學學求於迹也夫道一而已而學者之
用力異焉此君子所以當要其一也何也道根
於心善於身而宜於天下者也聖人之德王者
之業一而已而學之二者果足以背道邪夫學
以至乎聖人之道也是故以矜持入道道熟而
矜持泯矣以聞見識道道融而聞見黜矣又何
以見學之二哉今夫道固未嘗二也然自其體
段而言則謂之大發育萬物峻極于天是也自
punctuated:
同考試官教諭辛，批〔士子作此，雖皆知為存心致知，而不知其同歸於道。以道一為說，僅見此篇。〕
考試官學正王，批〔作理學論如此篇者絶少。〕
考試官教授許，批〔道一之說，諸作皆不能到。〕
學以盡道為極，道一而學有二焉，君子當要其所歸也。夫道者，率性而已，有二乎哉？而學者之法二之者，何也？不如是，不足以盡道也。道盡則無二矣。夫君子之學，主於盡道而已。道一而學二，以學之二而會道之一，君子奚病於學哉？尊德性而道問學，子思之言也。尊德性，學求於心也；道問學，學求於迹也。夫道一而已，而學者之用力異焉，此君子所以當要其一也。何也？道根於心，善於身，而宜於天下者也。聖人之德，王者之業，一而已，而學之二者，果足以背道邪？夫學以至乎聖人之道也。是故以矜持入道，道熟而矜持泯矣；以聞見識道，道融而聞見黜矣。又何以見學之二哉？今夫道固未嘗二也，然自其體段而言，則謂之大，發育萬物、峻極于天是也。自
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Xin, Instructor, comments: 〔Although the candidates writing on this subject all recognize that it concerns preserving the mind and extending knowledge, they do not understand that both converge upon the Way. Only this essay advances its argument through the unity of the Way.〕
Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: 〔Essays on the Learning of Principle such as this are exceedingly rare.〕
Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: 〔None of the other compositions attains this account of the unity of the Way.〕
Learning takes fully realizing the Way as its ultimate goal. The Way is one, yet learning has two approaches; the gentleman should grasp the common end toward which they lead. The Way is simply following one's nature: can there be two Ways? Why, then, do the methods of learning divide it into two? Without these approaches, one cannot fully realize the Way. Once the Way is fully realized, there is no duality. The gentleman's learning aims solely at fully realizing the Way. The Way is one, and learning has two approaches; through these two approaches he converges upon the unity of the Way. What difficulty, then, need the gentleman find in learning?
“Honor one's moral nature and pursue inquiry and learning”: these are Zisi's words. To honor one's moral nature is to seek learning within the mind; to pursue inquiry and learning is to seek it in outward manifestations. The Way is simply one, yet learners apply their efforts differently. This is why the gentleman must grasp their unity. Why is this so? The Way is rooted in the mind, manifests as goodness in one's person, and is fitting throughout the world. The virtue of the sage and the achievements of the true king are one and the same. Could the two approaches to learning really lead one away from the Way? Learning is the means of attaining the Way of the sages. Thus, one enters the Way through disciplined self-restraint, but once one's practice of the Way matures, deliberate restraint disappears. One recognizes the Way through what one hears and sees, but once one's understanding of the Way becomes fully integrated, such acquired knowledge is set aside. Where, then, can one still discern two approaches to learning?
Now, the Way has certainly never been two. Yet, speaking of its overall constitution, one calls it great: “It brings forth and nourishes the myriad things and rises to the very height of Heaven” expresses this. From …

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
温故也敦厚也所謂尊德性也盡精微也道中
庸也知新也崇禮也所謂道問學也尊德性所
以去欲而存其心心存而天下之理已具道問
學所以窮理而致其知知至而吾心之理愈充
是故其心合乎天地而無外其知周乎萬類而
無餘發育萬物峻極乎天吾之矩度也經禮三
百曲禮三千吾之經緯也根於心善於身宜於
天下矜持去而間見忘矣又知其孰為心孰為
迹孰為大孰為細哉由是處上下不違其道遇
===
治亂不失其時聖人之德已全而王者之業可
立也此君子存心致知之功豈可以強而能邪
甚矣心迹之不可判也清靜寂滅權謀術數異
端之學非聖人之道也然其始也無亦專求于
心獨泥其迹故其失之至此歟陸象山養性之
功多幾入于禪韓昌黎問學之功多不免因文
見道而已所學之偏重故也是二者可舉一而
廢一哉世之學者恐其學之不重于人也乃異
其說以欺天下高談性命遺絕世故歸之于杳
punctuated:
温故也，敦厚也，所謂尊德性也；盡精微也，道中庸也，知新也，崇禮也，所謂道問學也。尊德性，所以去欲而存其心，心存而天下之理已具；道問學，所以窮理而致其知，知至而吾心之理愈充。是故其心合乎天地而無外，其知周乎萬類而無餘。發育萬物，峻極乎天，吾之矩度也；經禮三百，曲禮三千，吾之經緯也。根於心，善於身，宜於天下，矜持去而間見忘矣。又知其孰為心，孰為迹，孰為大，孰為細哉？由是處上下不違其道，遇治亂不失其時，聖人之德已全，而王者之業可立也。此君子存心致知之功，豈可以強而能邪？

甚矣，心迹之不可判也！清靜寂滅，權謀術數，異端之學，非聖人之道也。然其始也，無亦專求于心，獨泥其迹，故其失之至此歟？陸象山養性之功多，幾入于禪；韓昌黎問學之功多，不免因文見道而已。所學之偏重故也。是二者，可舉一而廢一哉？世之學者，恐其學之不重于人也，乃異其說以欺天下，高談性命，遺絕世故，歸之于杳
translation_en:
…Reviewing the old and cultivating generosity and earnestness: these are what is meant by honoring one’s moral nature. Penetrating the finest subtleties, following the Mean, learning the new, and exalting ritual propriety: these are what is meant by pursuing inquiry and learning. Honoring one’s moral nature serves to eliminate desires and preserve the mind; once the mind is preserved, all the principles under Heaven are already present within it. Pursuing inquiry and learning serves to investigate principle exhaustively and extend one’s knowledge; once knowledge reaches its utmost, the principles within my mind become ever fuller. Thus one’s mind accords with Heaven and Earth, leaving nothing outside it, and one’s knowledge encompasses the myriad kinds of things, leaving nothing unaccounted for. Nurturing the myriad things and reaching to the heights of Heaven: these are my measures and standards. The three hundred major rites and three thousand detailed rules of ritual conduct: these are my warp and weft. Rooted in the mind, manifesting goodness in oneself, and fitting for all under Heaven, this cultivation leaves behind strained self-restraint and forgets partial insights [?]. How, then, could one still distinguish mind from outward manifestations, or the great from the minute? Accordingly, whether occupying a high or low position, one does not depart from the Way; whether encountering orderly or troubled times, one acts in keeping with the moment. The sage’s virtue is then complete, and the work of a true king can be established. Could this achievement of the gentleman in preserving the mind and extending knowledge be attained through force?

How utterly impossible it is to separate the mind from its outward manifestations! Purity and stillness, quiescent extinction, expedient stratagems, and manipulative techniques belong to heterodox teachings, not to the Way of the sages. Yet was it not that, at their beginnings, some sought exclusively within the mind while others clung solely to outward manifestations, so that their errors reached this point? Lu Xiangshan devoted much effort to nourishing his nature and came close to entering Chan Buddhism; Han Changli devoted much effort to inquiry and learning, yet could not go beyond perceiving the Way through literary writing. This resulted from the one-sided emphasis of their learning. Can one uphold either of these two approaches and discard the other? Scholars of the present age, fearing that their learning will not be esteemed by others, make their doctrines strange in order to deceive all under Heaven. They discourse loftily on human nature and destiny, abandon worldly affairs entirely, and consign everything to obscurity…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖德難名
神功若寂
兄弟世及以為禮
堯舜揖讓而得仁惟玆
曆數之歸爰遵
金匱之約
日華天表共瞻
有道之聖人
虎步龍行蚤識
===
太平之天子崇儒重道庸復先聖之家正藝昭
文經錫白鹿之洞褒田錫而作敢言之氣
任李覺而成迪德之譽賢俊滿
朝勳庸善世采葑菲之體識駑駘之途
命則維新人惟求舊念臣朴忠自許曾効勞
于
先皇知臣權倖所排頗畢忠于
今日再登客匆俄違朝請之班過被
寵光空懷家食之吉大疑大政入參
punctuated: 聖德難名，神功若寂。兄弟世及以為禮，堯舜揖讓而得仁。惟玆曆數之歸，爰遵金匱之約。日華天表，共瞻有道之聖人；虎步龍行，蚤識太平之天子。崇儒重道，庸復先聖之家；正藝昭文，經錫白鹿之洞。褒田錫而作敢言之氣，任李覺而成迪德之譽。賢俊滿朝，勳庸善世。采葑菲之體，識駑駘之途。命則維新，人惟求舊。念臣朴忠自許，曾効勞于先皇；知臣權倖所排，頗畢忠于今日。再登客匆，俄違朝請之班；過被寵光，空懷家食之吉。大疑大政，入參
translation_en:
Your sagely virtue is beyond naming; your divine achievements seem accomplished in silence. Succession from elder brother to younger accords with ritual propriety; the courteous yielding of Yao and Shun attained benevolence. As Heaven’s appointed succession has come to you, you have accordingly honored the compact of the Golden Coffer. In your sunlike radiance and heavenly bearing, all behold a sage possessed of the Way; in your tiger’s stride and dragon’s gait, they early recognized a Son of Heaven who would bring Great Peace. You honor Confucian learning and esteem the Way, restoring privileges to the household of the Former Sage. You rectify the arts and illuminate culture [?], bestowing canonical books upon the White Deer Grotto Academy. By commending Tian Xi, you encouraged the spirit of fearless speech; by employing Li Jue, you earned praise for advancing virtue. Worthy and talented men fill your court, and their meritorious service benefits the world. You follow the principle of gathering turnips and radishes without rejecting them for their roots, and recognize that even inferior horses have their uses [?]. Though the mandate is renewed, it is men of longstanding service whom you seek.

You recall that I, your servant, have prided myself on simple loyalty and once rendered service to the late emperor. You know that I was excluded by powerful favorites, yet have devoted my loyalty to the present reign. Again I came to the guest’s window [?], but soon departed from the ranks attending court. Favored beyond my deserts by your gracious regard, I vainly cherished the good fortune of taking my meals at home. In great uncertainties and great affairs of government, I enter to participate in …

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
廟圖斯謨斯猷出惟
后德蓋論語半部爭托諸空言而犬馬餘生必
竭其素力尚賴鼎鐺有耳孰謂樞軸無機
矜名位而伐功勞服膺
聖戒舉賢能而明賞罰懋勵初心上以凝
宗社奠安之休下弗為子孫恩澤之計伏願
任賢勿貳納諫如流
大度有容
神武不殺春秋大一統亟收取漢之功卑書
===
正萬邦允惟纘禹之服
天地交而成泰陽長陰消
神人助而得尊遏惡揚善臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策
punctuated:
廟圖，斯謨斯猷，出惟后德。蓋《論語》半部，爭托諸空言？而犬馬餘生，必竭其素力。尚賴鼎鐺有耳，孰謂樞軸無機？矜名位而伐功勞，服膺聖戒；舉賢能而明賞罰，懋勵初心。上以凝宗社奠安之休，下弗為子孫恩澤之計。伏願任賢勿貳，納諫如流，大度有容，神武不殺。《春秋》大一統，亟收取漢之功；卑書正萬邦，允惟纘禹之服。天地交而成泰，陽長陰消；神人助而得尊，遏惡揚善。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁場
策
translation_en:
…the deliberations of the imperial council: these plans and counsels issue solely from Your Majesty’s virtue. As for half of the Analects, how could I entrust it to empty words [?]? Throughout the remaining years of this servant’s life, I shall certainly exert all the strength I have. I still rely upon the cauldron’s having ears; who would say that the central pivot has no mechanism? I take to heart Your Majesty’s warning against priding oneself on rank and boasting of achievements. In promoting the worthy and capable and making rewards and punishments clear, I shall strive to uphold my original resolve. Above, I seek to consolidate the blessing of security for the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain; below, I shall not scheme to obtain favors for my descendants.

I humbly pray that you employ the worthy without wavering and accept remonstrance as readily as water flows; that your magnanimity embrace all, and your divine martial power prevail without killing. The Spring and Autumn Annals exalts great unity: may you swiftly achieve the merit of taking Han [?]. The Documents [?] speaks of setting the myriad states in order: truly may you continue Yu’s undertaking. Heaven and earth interact to produce Peace, with yang increasing and yin diminishing; spirits and men lend their aid to secure your exalted position, as you restrain evil and promote good. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sageliness, cannot contain his intense emotion and deepest trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude and make it known to Your Majesty.

Third Session
Policy Essays

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
第一問　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　吳三樂
同考試官教諭劉　批〔收要一書出臣下輯錄我〕
祖宗言行政事之大者其間若足食足兵又
今日之急務是作鋪張有體忠蓋藹然置之高等良協輿論噫吾之知子
以文也此殆未盡子之蘊焉尚撼忠丁
同考試官教諭辛　批〔政要四事非涵泳〕
大廷之對
聖化而有得者不能揄揚若是是以取之
===
考試官學正王　批
聖祖之法今時之務敷陳有條必通達國體者
考試官教授許　批〔語朴意宛善言〕
祖訓者
立法以垂後者未有不善之法守法以紹
統者當有不易之守立法無不善者慮之
周也守法不容易者行之利也故曰遵先
王之法而過者未之有也此
聖祖神宗貽謀之遠我
punctuated:
第一問　吳三樂

同考試官教諭劉批〔收要一書，出臣下輯錄我〕祖宗言行政事之大者，其間若足食足兵，又今日之急務。是作鋪張有體，忠蓋藹然，置之高等，良協輿論。噫！吾之知子以文也，此殆未盡子之蘊焉，尚撼忠丁。

同考試官教諭辛批〔政要四事，非涵泳〕大廷之對，聖化而有得者，不能揄揚若是，是以取之。

考試官學正王批：聖祖之法，今時之務，敷陳有條，必通達國體者。

考試官教授許批〔語朴意宛，善言〕祖訓者。

立法以垂後者，未有不善之法；守法以紹統者，當有不易之守。立法無不善者，慮之周也；守法不容易者，行之利也。故曰：「遵先王之法而過者，未之有也。」此聖祖神宗貽謀之遠，我
translation_en:
First policy question — Wu Sanle 吳三樂

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu 劉, Instructor: “The book Shouyao [?] was compiled by subjects who collected the major words, deeds, and affairs of government of our imperial ancestors. Among these, ensuring sufficient food and sufficient troops are also urgent tasks today. This composition develops its subject with proper form, and its loyalty is abundantly evident [?]. Placing it in a high grade accords well with the general judgment. Ah! I know you through your writing, yet this probably does not exhaust what you have within you. [Concluding words unclear: 尚撼忠丁.]”

Comment by Associate Examiner Xin 辛, Instructor: “The four matters concerning the essentials of government—unless one has immersed oneself in the sage ruler’s transforming influence and gained something from it, one cannot extol them thus. For this reason I selected it.” The words “response at the great court” (大廷之對) interrupt the transmitted text here [?].

Comment by Examiner Wang 王, Director of Studies: “The laws of the sagely progenitor and the tasks of the present age are set forth in orderly fashion. The author must be someone thoroughly conversant with the principles of government.”

Comment by Examiner Xu 許, Professor: “The language is plain and the meaning subtly expressed; the author discusses the Ancestral Instructions well.”

When laws are established to be handed down to posterity, none of those laws is other than good; when laws are upheld to continue the imperial succession, their observance ought to remain unchanging. That the laws established are all good results from comprehensive deliberation; that their observance does not readily change results from the benefits of putting them into practice. Thus it is said: “There has never been anyone who followed the laws of the former kings and went astray.” Such is the far-reaching foresight of the plans bequeathed by the sagely progenitors and divine ancestors, our…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
躬耕以勸農親蠶以率織慮俗之侈也下
詔以禁之憂歲之凶也積粟以備之
神武素揚于沙漠遠夷寒心
天兵近出于邊陲叛賊獻首執事猶以財乏歲
凶兵弱邊患為憂者圖治無窮之心也然
祖宗之法亦豈無可申明于
今日者乎傳曰無戎而城仇必保焉善治國
者不患無臨事之謀而患無先事之備
聖天子躬行節儉矣而軍國之冗費或未裁也
===
存心荒政矣而四方水旱之報則未已也
武備雖不乏用然國中之兵久忘鋒鏑聞
戰則懼況用之乎邊疆雖皆保完然夷狄
為中國患自古為然可一日無備乎嘗觀
事有出于天下之所共知衆人之所共言
者聽其言皆尋常而無奇異之論然不如
是則不足以集事為今之計亦惟曰以
祖宗之法申明遵行之而已無虞之世儆戒存
焉安不忘危則然也惟執事者圖之
punctuated:
躬耕以勸農，親蠶以率織。慮俗之侈也，下詔以禁之；憂歲之凶也，積粟以備之。神武素揚于沙漠，遠夷寒心；天兵近出于邊陲，叛賊獻首。執事猶以財乏、歲凶、兵弱、邊患為憂者，圖治無窮之心也。然祖宗之法，亦豈無可申明于今日者乎？傳曰：「無戎而城，仇必保焉。」善治國者，不患無臨事之謀，而患無先事之備。
聖天子躬行節儉矣，而軍國之冗費或未裁也；存心荒政矣，而四方水旱之報則未已也。武備雖不乏用，然國中之兵久忘鋒鏑，聞戰則懼，況用之乎？邊疆雖皆保完，然夷狄為中國患，自古為然，可一日無備乎？嘗觀事有出于天下之所共知、衆人之所共言者，聽其言，皆尋常而無奇異之論，然不如是則不足以集事。為今之計，亦惟曰以祖宗之法申明遵行之而已。無虞之世，儆戒存焉，安不忘危則然也。惟執事者圖之。
translation_en:
…He personally plows to encourage agriculture and personally tends silkworms to lead the way in weaving. Concerned about extravagance in popular customs, he issues edicts prohibiting it; worried about crop failures, he stores grain in preparation. His divine martial might has long been renowned throughout the desert, striking fear into distant foreign peoples; imperial troops have recently advanced to the frontier, and rebel heads have been presented. That you, sir, nevertheless remain concerned about depleted finances, crop failures, weak troops, and frontier troubles shows your unceasing commitment to good government. Yet surely there are also laws of the imperial ancestors that could be clarified and reaffirmed today? The Commentary says: “Fortify a city when there is no war, and enemies will surely occupy it.” Those skilled in governing a state worry less about lacking a plan when trouble arises than about lacking preparations before it comes.
The sagely Son of Heaven personally practices frugality, yet superfluous military and state expenditures may still remain uncurtailed. He gives thought to famine relief, yet reports of floods and droughts from all quarters have not ceased. Although military resources are not insufficient for use, the troops within the realm have long forgotten blades and arrows. They fear the very mention of battle; how, then, could they be deployed? Although the frontiers have all been preserved intact, foreign peoples have troubled China since antiquity. Can we go even one day without preparations? I have observed that some measures arise from what everyone under Heaven knows and what people commonly say. Their proposals sound entirely ordinary, containing no extraordinary ideas; yet without proceeding in this way, nothing can be accomplished. The plan for the present can only be to clarify and reaffirm the laws of the imperial ancestors and carry them out. Even in an age free from troubles, vigilance must endure: this is what it means not to forget danger in times of peace. I ask you, sir, to consider this.

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
無疑權其宜法行而不背此周禮一書所
以可用於
今日也請因明問而復之天高地下禮制興
馬禮者理也故曰治定而後制禮周禮一
書周公所作也損益夏商之制斟酌文武
之規以冢宰掌邦治司徒掌邦教宗伯掌
邦禮司馬掌邦政司寇掌邦禁司空掌邦
土每卿六十屬凡百司庶務以及百工技
藝無不備焉以三百六十而歸于六以六
===
而統於一故曰辨方定位體國經野設官
分職以為民極者也朱子曰周公致太平
之書信乎非聖人不能作也或者以為文
王治岐之書不知郊祀之典封建之制果
侯國所行者哉或者曰成周理財之書然
倡九牧阜兆民豈專為理財而已哉若夫
公孤之官不列而朝巡之制不載與周官
異者則亦有說也蓋周官者史臣紀成王
訓迪百官之詞故惟備其大體周禮者周
punctuated: 無疑，權其宜，法行而不背，此《周禮》一書所以可用於今日也。請因明問而復之。天高地下，禮制興馬。禮者，理也。故曰：「治定而後制禮。」《周禮》一書，周公所作也。損益夏商之制，斟酌文武之規，以冢宰掌邦治，司徒掌邦教，宗伯掌邦禮，司馬掌邦政，司寇掌邦禁，司空掌邦土。每卿六十屬，凡百司庶務，以及百工技藝，無不備焉。以三百六十而歸于六，以六而統於一。故曰：「辨方定位，體國經野，設官分職，以為民極者也。」朱子曰：「周公致太平之書。」信乎，非聖人不能作也。或者以為文王治岐之書，不知郊祀之典、封建之制，果侯國所行者哉？或者曰成周理財之書，然倡九牧、阜兆民，豈專為理財而已哉？若夫公孤之官不列，而朝巡之制不載，與《周官》異者，則亦有說也。蓋《周官》者，史臣紀成王訓迪百官之詞，故惟備其大體；《周禮》者，周
translation_en:
…without doubt; weighing what is appropriate, the regulations can be implemented without contravention. This is why the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) can be applied today. Allow me to respond to your discerning question. Heaven is high and earth is low, and ritual institutions arise [?]. Ritual is principle. Thus it is said: “Only after order has been established are rites instituted.”

The Rites of Zhou was composed by the Duke of Zhou. He made additions to and subtractions from the institutions of Xia and Shang, and weighed the precedents of Kings Wen and Wu. The Minister of State oversaw the administration of the realm; the Minister of Education, its instruction; the Minister of Rites, its rituals; the Minister of War, its military affairs; the Minister of Justice, its prohibitions; and the Minister of Works, its lands. Each minister had sixty subordinate offices. All the manifold affairs of the various offices, down to the skills and techniques of the hundred crafts, were provided for. The three hundred and sixty offices were grouped under six, and the six were united under one. Thus it is said: “He distinguished the directions and fixed positions, laid out the capital and divided the countryside, established offices and apportioned duties, thereby providing a standard for the people.” Master Zhu said: “This is the book through which the Duke of Zhou brought about supreme peace.” Truly, none but a sage could have composed it.

Some regard it as a book concerning King Wen’s government of Qi. But they fail to understand: were the rites of suburban sacrifice and the institutions for enfeoffing lords really matters that a feudal state could undertake? Others call it a book on financial administration at Chengzhou. Yet to lead the governors of the nine regions and enrich the myriad people—could this concern financial administration alone?

As for its omission of the offices of the Three Dukes and Three Solitary Dignitaries, and its failure to record the institutions of court audiences and inspection tours, thus differing from the “Officers of Zhou” (Zhouguan), there is an explanation for this too. The “Officers of Zhou” is the court historians’ record of King Cheng’s words instructing and guiding the hundred officials, and therefore sets out only the general framework. The Rites of Zhou, however, is the Duke of Zhou’s…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
公課責百官之法故獨詳其細事特非此
邪冬官本缺劉德以考工記補之好古博
雅固可取也然審曲面埶之法材美工巧
之論與居四民時地利者果可同哉周禮
無傳鄭玄註之引用緯書固可議也然發
明制作之意豈可少哉或以為漢儒附會
之書正以有見劉鄭二君子之為而不能
不為之疑也若使全出漢儒之手則冬官
之缺奚用考工記補哉蓋是書壞散于秦
火補緝于漢儒非全書也又何足深疑乎
夫有關雎麟趾之意而可以行周官之法
度逆莽宇文泰之輩不足道矣王仲淹模
倣舊文而自比孔子禮豈可以偽為乎唐
太宗詳于制度而略于綱常禮不可以虛
行也豈書之罪哉我
朝建官臺閣之設即周公孤之體也六部之
設即周六卿之制也而其間有不盡同者
古今之勢異也故曰五帝不相襲禮三王
punctuated: 公課責百官之法，故獨詳其細事，特非此邪？冬官本缺，劉德以《考工記》補之，好古博雅，固可取也。然審曲面埶之法、材美工巧之論，與居四民、時地利者，果可同哉？《周禮》無傳，鄭玄註之，引用緯書，固可議也。然發明制作之意，豈可少哉？或以為漢儒附會之書，正以有見劉、鄭二君子之為，而不能不為之疑也。若使全出漢儒之手，則冬官之缺，奚用《考工記》補哉？蓋是書壞散于秦火，補緝于漢儒，非全書也，又何足深疑乎？夫有《關雎》《麟趾》之意，而可以行《周官》之法度。逆莽、宇文泰之輩，不足道矣。王仲淹模倣舊文而自比孔子，禮豈可以偽為乎？唐太宗詳于制度而略于綱常，禮不可以虛行也，豈書之罪哉？我朝建官，臺閣之設，即周公孤之體也；六部之設，即周六卿之制也。而其間有不盡同者，古今之勢異也。故曰：「五帝不相襲禮，三王
translation_en:
…the Duke of Zhou’s rules for assessing and holding the hundred officials accountable; hence it gives particular attention to the details of their duties. Is this not precisely the distinction? The section on the Winter Offices was originally missing, and Liu De supplied the Record of Artificers (Kaogong ji) to fill the gap. His love of antiquity and extensive learning certainly deserve appreciation. Yet can methods for examining curves and surfaces, and discussions of fine materials and skilled craftsmanship, really be equated with settling the four classes of people and utilizing the land’s resources at the proper seasons?

The Rites of Zhou (Zhou li) had no transmitted commentary, so Zheng Xuan annotated it. His citations of apocryphal texts are certainly open to criticism. Yet can his elucidation of the intentions behind its institutions be dispensed with? Some regard it as a work cobbled together by Han scholars. It is precisely because they have seen what the two gentlemen Liu and Zheng did that they cannot help doubting it. If it had been entirely the work of Han scholars, however, why would they have needed the Record of Artificers to fill the missing Winter Offices? This book was damaged and scattered in the Qin book burning, then supplemented and pieced together by Han scholars. It is not a complete text; why, then, should this provoke such profound doubt?

Only with the spirit of “The Ospreys” (Guanju) and “The Qilin’s Hooves” (Linzhi) can one put into practice the laws and standards of the Offices of Zhou (Zhou guan). Such men as the rebel Wang Mang and Yuwen Tai are not worth discussing. Wang Zhongyan imitated ancient writings and compared himself to Confucius—but can ritual propriety be fabricated? Emperor Taizong of Tang attended closely to institutions but gave scant attention to the cardinal bonds and constant moral principles. Ritual propriety cannot be practiced as an empty form. How could this be the book’s fault?

In establishing offices, our dynasty’s provision of the Censorate and Grand Secretariat embodies the arrangement of the Three Dukes and Three Solitaries of Zhou; its establishment of the Six Ministries follows the system of Zhou’s six ministers. Where the arrangements are not entirely identical, this is because circumstances differ between antiquity and the present. Thus it is said: “The Five Emperors did not inherit one another’s rites; the Three Kings …

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
不相沿樂況至今十
國家承平既久正制禮作樂光明德業之時
執事欲行周禮于今是也愚謂禮者得其
理而已泥古不適俗儒之陋也隨時變易
聖人之道也周公居古其禮如此使周公
居今其禮未可知也是故親踈有等尊卑
有分則禮行于家矣君攬其權臣承其令
大吏持其綱小吏分其紀則禮行于國矣
萬國奉命四夷不侵民安其業物遂其性
則禮行于天下矣今之禮即古之禮也叔
孫通之綿蕞將安施哉不識執事以為然
否
第三問
同考試官訓導余 批〔性學一題正以觀士子平日涵養體認之學此篇以孟子言氣為疑備朱子論學為不偏皆鑿鑿〕
王堯言
同考試官教諭趙 批〔此策言性學一以孟氏朱子為有據非剿空支設者可以録之以釋疑惑〕
punctuated:
不相沿樂，況至今十！國家承平既久，正制禮作樂、光明德業之時。執事欲行周禮于今，是也。愚謂禮者，得其理而已。泥古不適，俗儒之陋也；隨時變易，聖人之道也。周公居古，其禮如此；使周公居今，其禮未可知也。是故親踈有等，尊卑有分，則禮行于家矣；君攬其權，臣承其令，大吏持其綱，小吏分其紀，則禮行于國矣；萬國奉命，四夷不侵，民安其業，物遂其性，則禮行于天下矣。今之禮，即古之禮也。叔孫通之綿蕞，將安施哉？不識執事以為然否？
第三問
同考試官訓導余，批〔性學一題，正以觀士子平日涵養體認之學。此篇以孟子言氣為疑，備朱子論學為不偏，皆鑿鑿。〕
王堯言
同考試官教諭趙，批〔此策言性學，一以孟氏、朱子為有據，非剿空支設者，可以録之以釋疑惑。〕
translation_en:
…did not follow one another in music, how much more so down to the present [?]! Our state has long enjoyed peace; this is precisely the time to establish rites and create music, making its virtue and achievements shine forth. You wish to implement the Rites of Zhou today, and rightly so. In my humble view, ritual requires only that one grasp its underlying principles. Clinging to antiquity without adapting is the failing of commonplace scholars; changing with the times is the Way of the sages. The Duke of Zhou lived in antiquity, and his rites took that form. If he lived today, we cannot know what form his rites would take. Thus, when degrees of closeness and distance in kinship are observed, and distinctions between superior and inferior maintained, ritual prevails within the family. When the ruler holds authority and his ministers obey his commands, when senior officials maintain the main framework and junior officials attend to its particulars, ritual prevails within the state. When the myriad states obey commands, the peoples of the four quarters do not invade, the people pursue their livelihoods in peace, and all things fulfill their natures, ritual prevails throughout the realm. The rites of today are thus the rites of antiquity. What use, then, would there be for Shusun Tong’s ritual rehearsals with bundles of reeds? I do not know whether you consider this correct.
Third Question
Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The question on the learning of human nature is intended precisely to assess the candidates’ habitual work of inner cultivation and experiential understanding. This essay raises doubts about Mengzi’s discussion of qi and treats Master Zhu’s discussion of learning as free from partiality [?]. Its points are all firmly grounded.〕
Wang Yaoyan
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: 〔In discussing the learning of human nature, this policy essay consistently takes Mengzi and Master Zhu as authoritative grounds. It is no exercise in empty borrowing and contrivance; it may be included to resolve doubts and confusion.〕

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
察聖賢救世之志徒據其問答之迹而不
知其言之不終肆者孰非孟氏廻瀾之力
也自是以還精一學熄分門對壘竟失所
歸朱子乃取語孟六經諸書而訓釋之使
學者有所憑藉以為學問思辨之地而不
陷於荊棘榛莽之塗則其措之行也必矣
草廬吳氏乃謂其道問學之功居多而以
象山陸氏尊德性方之是徒見其著述之
詳而不察其憂深慮遠之意習聞乎頓悟
===
之說而不知博學詳說者所以為蓄德之
地也自今觀之周子以義直斷嚴幹固為
剛善猛隘強梁為剛惡又以慈巽順為柔
善懦弱無斷邪佞為柔惡俾人自易其惡
以至於中為其性附於氣質之中所以不
能無數者之別由其性體之本善是皆可
以變其異而反乎同也而執事又以皐陶
九德箕子三德例舉並言于此尤可見乎
人之德多寡大小莫非天質而聖人之感
punctuated:
察聖賢救世之志，徒據其問答之迹，而不知其言之不終肆者，孰非孟氏廻瀾之力也？自是以還，精一學熄，分門對壘，竟失所歸。朱子乃取語孟六經諸書而訓釋之，使學者有所憑藉，以為學問思辨之地，而不陷於荊棘榛莽之塗，則其措之行也必矣。草廬吳氏乃謂其道問學之功居多，而以象山陸氏尊德性方之。是徒見其著述之詳，而不察其憂深慮遠之意，習聞乎頓悟之說，而不知博學詳說者所以為蓄德之地也。
自今觀之，周子以義、直、斷、嚴、幹、固為剛善，猛、隘、強梁為剛惡；又以慈、巽、順為柔善，懦弱、無斷、邪佞為柔惡。俾人自易其惡，以至於中。為其性附於氣質之中，所以不能無數者之別；由其性體之本善，是皆可以變其異而反乎同也。而執事又以皐陶九德、箕子三德例舉並言于此，尤可見乎人之德多寡大小莫非天質，而聖人之感
translation_en:
…to discern the resolve of the sages and worthies to save the world, merely relying on the traces of their questions and answers, without understanding that their words did not ultimately run unchecked [?]—was this not all due to Mengzi’s power to turn back the tide? Thereafter, the learning of refinement and single-mindedness died out; separate schools formed opposing camps and ultimately lost sight of their proper destination. Master Zhu then took the Analects, the Mencius, the Six Classics, and other books and explicated them, giving students something to rely upon as a basis for study, inquiry, reflection, and discrimination. By keeping them from straying onto paths overgrown with thorns and brush, he ensured that they would put their learning into practice. Yet Wu Caolu claimed that Master Zhu’s achievement lay chiefly in pursuing inquiry and learning, and contrasted him with Lu Xiangshan’s honoring of the moral nature. This is merely to notice the detail of his writings without discerning the depth of his concern and the reach of his foresight; it is to be accustomed to hearing doctrines of sudden enlightenment without knowing that broad learning and detailed exposition provide the ground for nurturing virtue.
Viewed from the present, Master Zhou classified righteousness, uprightness, decisiveness, strictness, capability, and firmness as good forms of strength, and fierceness, narrowness, and overbearing force as bad forms of strength. He likewise classified kindness, modest compliance, and gentleness as good forms of softness, and weakness, indecision, perversity, and flattery as bad forms of softness. He sought to have people change their own faults and thereby attain the mean. Because their nature inheres in their material endowment, these several distinctions necessarily exist. Yet because the substance of their nature is originally good, they can all transform what differs and return to what is shared. Moreover, you, sir, have adduced Gao Yao’s nine virtues and Jizi’s three virtues together as examples here. This makes it especially clear that people’s virtues, whether many or few, great or small, all derive from their natural endowment, while the sage’s influence…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
楊中立之學力深矣而晝壯趾於權姦之
門明辨練習邢明叔之天資美矣而終濡
首於禪學之陋過化便所存者神存神便
所過者化顯道之言似簡切而有味也然
不若性性為能存神物物為能過化為足
以形容王道之大由誠而至於明由明而
至於誠子厚之訓似質實而近理也然不
若誠則明矣明則誠矣為足以發明天道
之純謝氏景温本非能通易者也而程子
===
以通易許之特取其能虛以受人焉爾非
謂其能知變化之道也劉質夫本非能傳
春秋者也而程子以作傳屬之特以其能
篤信果行焉爾非謂其能通聖人之藴也
自下學以至上達天德謝氏之見聖道不
可謂不大矣然於一貫之旨亦豈能深知
其妙讀其書已能不逆於心游氏之語訂
頑不可謂不速矣然於中庸之理亦安能
悉會其全邵子洛中四賢之詠固非甚為
punctuated:
楊中立之學力深矣，而晝壯趾於權姦之門。明辨練習，邢明叔之天資美矣，而終濡首於禪學之陋。「過化便所存者神，存神便所過者化」，顯道之言似簡切而有味也，然不若「性性為能存神，物物為能過化」為足以形容王道之大。「由誠而至於明，由明而至於誠」，子厚之訓似質實而近理也，然不若「誠則明矣，明則誠矣」為足以發明天道之純。

謝氏景温本非能通易者也，而程子以通易許之，特取其能虛以受人焉爾，非謂其能知變化之道也。劉質夫本非能傳春秋者也，而程子以作傳屬之，特以其能篤信果行焉爾，非謂其能通聖人之藴也。

自下學以至上達天德，謝氏之見聖道不可謂不大矣，然於一貫之旨，亦豈能深知其妙？讀其書已能不逆於心，游氏之語訂頑不可謂不速矣，然於中庸之理，亦安能悉會其全？邵子洛中四賢之詠，固非甚為
translation_en:
Yang Zhongli’s learning was indeed profound, yet he boldly advanced to the gate of a powerful, treacherous minister [?]. Possessed of clear discernment and practiced understanding, Xing Mingshu had excellent natural gifts, yet ultimately became submerged in the narrowness of Chan Buddhist learning. “To transform wherever one passes is precisely to be numinous wherever one abides; to preserve the numinous is precisely to transform wherever one passes”: Xiandao’s words seem concise, pertinent, and rich in meaning. Yet they do not express the greatness of the kingly Way as fully as “Fully realizing one’s nature enables one to preserve the numinous; treating each thing according to its nature enables one to transform wherever one passes.” “Proceeding from sincerity to understanding, and from understanding to sincerity”: Zihou’s teaching seems substantial and close to principle. Yet it does not elucidate the purity of the Way of Heaven as fully as “With sincerity comes understanding; with understanding comes sincerity.”

Xie Jingwen was not, in fact, someone who thoroughly understood the Book of Changes. When Master Cheng credited him with understanding it, he was merely commending his capacity to empty himself and receive instruction from others; he did not mean that Xie understood the Way of change and transformation. Liu Zhifu was not, in fact, someone capable of writing a commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals. When Master Cheng entrusted him with writing one, it was merely because he was steadfast in belief and resolute in action; he did not mean that Liu comprehended the sage’s profound meaning.

From learning matters here below to attaining an understanding of Heaven’s virtue above: Master Xie’s vision of the sages’ Way cannot be called anything but broad. Yet could he deeply understand the subtle meaning of the single thread running through it all? Merely upon reading the text, he already found nothing in it contrary to his own mind: Master You’s response to Correcting Insensitivity (Dingwan) cannot be called anything but swift. Yet how could he fully comprehend the entirety of the principles of the Doctrine of the Mean? Master Shao’s poem on the four worthies of Luoyang was certainly not excessively …

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
溢美者也然彥國諸人奚可與伯淳並稱
謝氏游楊見愛之論固非虛為獻諛者也
然中立定夫亦豈有二程氣象思叔以篤
識入道而後逸之稱乃慮其師辟之過彥
明以篤行為學而終守之論亦與其參魯
之賢以主一為敬而告之和叔以直內用
敬而告之彥明其意互相發明而其言亦
各有攸當也至於叔子以嚴重自處嘗自
嘆不及其兄而師道亦因以為重伯子嘗
===
和易可親衆皆悅而從之而後學成就為
居多明道嘗曰顥接人多矣其不雜者三
人豈非以子厚堯夫司馬君實皆醇乎其
醇者乎言三人則其他之弗醇也可見矣
伊川嘗曰我死而不失其正者惟尹氏之
子豈非以彥明之學獨得其宗而不流於
異端者乎言尹氏則其他之弗正也可識
矣至於伊洛之所以為教也又有可言者
焉誠敬以為入門踐履以為實地自致知
punctuated:
溢美者也，然彥國諸人奚可與伯淳並稱？謝氏游楊見愛之論，固非虛為獻諛者也，然中立定夫亦豈有二程氣象？思叔以篤識入道，而後逸之稱，乃慮其師辟之過；彥明以篤行為學，而終守之論，亦與其參魯之賢。以主一為敬，而告之和叔；以直內用敬，而告之彥明。其意互相發明，而其言亦各有攸當也。至於叔子以嚴重自處，嘗自嘆不及其兄，而師道亦因以為重；伯子嘗和易可親，衆皆悅而從之，而後學成就為居多。
明道嘗曰：「顥接人多矣，其不雜者三人。」豈非以子厚堯夫司馬君實皆醇乎其醇者乎？言三人，則其他之弗醇也可見矣。伊川嘗曰：「我死而不失其正者，惟尹氏之子。」豈非以彥明之學獨得其宗，而不流於異端者乎？言尹氏，則其他之弗正也可識矣。
至於伊洛之所以為教也，又有可言者焉。誠敬以為入門，踐履以為實地，自致知
translation_en:
…excessive praise; yet how could Yanguo and the others be ranked alongside Bochun? Master Xie’s remarks about You and Yang being loved were certainly no empty flattery; yet did Zhongli and Dingfu possess the bearing of the two Cheng masters? Sishu entered the Way through firm understanding, but the remark that he later grew lax expressed concern over his fault of following his own prejudices [?]. Yanming pursued learning through steadfast practice, and the judgment that he would hold fast to the end likewise acknowledged his worth as one who possessed Zeng Shen’s apparent dullness. To Heshu, the teaching was that reverence consists in concentrating on one thing; to Yanming, it was that reverence is employed to straighten the inner self. These ideas illuminate one another, while each formulation was suited to its recipient. As for the younger Cheng master, he conducted himself with stern gravity and once lamented that he fell short of his elder brother; yet this also lent weight to his authority as a teacher. The elder Cheng master was affable and approachable; all gladly followed him, and those among his later students who achieved success were more numerous.
Mingdao once said: “I, Hao, have dealt with many people. Three of them are free of admixture.” Was this not because Zihou, Yaofu, and Sima Junshi were all pure in their purity? By specifying three, he made it apparent that the others were not pure. Yichuan once said: “After I die, the only one who will not depart from rectitude is the son of the Yin family.” Was this not because Yanming alone had grasped the essential foundation of his teaching and did not drift into heterodoxy? By specifying the son of the Yin family, he made it possible to recognize that the others would not maintain rectitude.
As for the teaching of the Yi–Luo school, there is still more to say. Sincerity and reverence provide the entrance; putting learning into practice provides the firm ground. From extending knowledge…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
而至於知止自誠意而至於平天下自洒
掃應對而至於窮理盡性是真有以發明
堯舜以來相傳心法之要而衍道統於無
窮也惜乎游楊諸人不能逮肖之爾雖然
不有以作之孰從而述之不有以繼之孰
從而傳之是故道學之統孟子而後有周
子以繼其絕至程子而始著由程子而後
得游楊諸人以繼其微至朱子而始全是
以吾道之在天下炳乎如日月麗天沛乎
===
如江河行地而人不昧於所趨也愚也生
長於伊洛道學之區上遇我
國家道化之盛又惡敢不以學之深者自勵
而言之不純惟執事者擇焉
第五問
同考試官教諭張 批 〔春秋洪範言雖弗同〕
而義實表裏後儒𩔖言忘味緣飾災變惑上誣下
李檀
流弊滋甚子能究析其藴惓惓以堯湯望
punctuated:
而至於知止，自誠意而至於平天下，自洒掃應對而至於窮理盡性，是真有以發明堯舜以來相傳心法之要，而衍道統於無窮也。惜乎游楊諸人不能逮肖之爾！雖然，不有以作之，孰從而述之？不有以繼之，孰從而傳之？是故道學之統，孟子而後有周子以繼其絕，至程子而始著；由程子而後，得游楊諸人以繼其微，至朱子而始全。是以吾道之在天下，炳乎如日月麗天，沛乎如江河行地，而人不昧於所趨也。愚也生長於伊洛道學之區，上遇我國家道化之盛，又惡敢不以學之深者自勵？而言之不純，惟執事者擇焉。

第五問

同考試官教諭張批：〔春秋洪範言雖弗同〕而義實表裏。後儒𩔖言忘味，緣飾災變，惑上誣下。

李檀

流弊滋甚，子能究析其藴，惓惓以堯湯望
translation_en:
…and proceeds to knowing where to stop; from making the intentions sincere to bringing peace to all under Heaven; and from sprinkling and sweeping, answering and responding, to fully investigating principle and fulfilling one’s nature. This truly illuminates the essentials of the teaching of the mind transmitted since Yao and Shun, extending the succession of the Way without end. It is regrettable that You, Yang, and the others could not measure up to their masters! Yet without someone to initiate it, who could follow and expound it? Without someone to continue it, who could follow and transmit it? Thus, in the succession of Learning of the Way, after Mengzi, Master Zhou restored the broken line, and only with the Cheng masters did it become manifest. After the Cheng masters, You, Yang, and the others sustained it in its weakness, and only with Master Zhu did it become complete. Hence our Way shines throughout the world like the sun and moon set in Heaven, and flows abundantly like rivers coursing over the earth, so that people are not ignorant of the direction they should take. I, ignorant though I am, was born and raised in the Yi and Luo region, the home of Learning of the Way, and have had the good fortune to live amid our dynasty’s flourishing transformation through the Way. How could I dare fail to spur myself toward deeper learning? As for any impurity in my words, I leave it to you, the examiners, to judge.

Fifth Policy Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔“Although the wording of the Spring and Autumn Annals and the ‘Great Plan’ differs,〕 their meanings are complementary, like outer and inner aspects of the same thing. Later Confucians grouped sayings together but forgot their savor [?], embellishing accounts of calamities and anomalies, misleading those above and deceiving those below.

Li Tan

“The resulting abuses have grown ever more severe. You have been able to investigate and analyze the underlying meanings, earnestly hoping that Yao and Tang will serve as models for…”

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖明可謂忠敬之士豈徒其文之可録哉
考試官學正王 批〔窮詰數子無所用辯仲尼之徒皇極之臣爾固其人乎〕
考試官教授許 批〔能達天人之理取之〕
人君之治天下莫先於辯天人之理而識
其感通之幾卒然而值莫知其端或合或
離竟無以遁其情幾之謂也形殊而勢懸
外若暌逆而其生化消息潛通而默運弗
間毫髮則其理之一也知其理之一而所
===
以察其幾者將不外是而得之矣慨自仲
尼殁而大道弗明於天下由是諸子各以
其意之所見援古摧今肆其頰舌自謂明
於天人之際甚析也然孰於有者昧其理
之一淪於無者弗察其機之神類皆眩術
逞數雜以符命讖緯詭怪之言方其偶合
億中則固可信可愕徐求其故而不得凡
天下大異殊祥關于理亂皆將視為適然
之故蠹治害政可勝言哉方今
punctuated:
聖明，可謂忠敬之士，豈徒其文之可録哉！
考試官學正王批〔窮詰數子，無所用辯。仲尼之徒，皇極之臣，爾固其人乎？〕
考試官教授許批〔能達天人之理，取之。〕
人君之治天下，莫先於辯天人之理，而識其感通之幾。卒然而值，莫知其端；或合或離，竟無以遁其情，幾之謂也。形殊而勢懸，外若暌逆，而其生化消息，潛通而默運，弗間毫髮，則其理之一也。知其理之一，而所以察其幾者，將不外是而得之矣。慨自仲尼殁，而大道弗明於天下，由是諸子各以其意之所見，援古摧今，肆其頰舌，自謂明於天人之際甚析也。然孰於有者，昧其理之一；淪於無者，弗察其機之神。類皆眩術逞數，雜以符命讖緯詭怪之言。方其偶合億中，則固可信可愕；徐求其故而不得，凡天下大異殊祥，關于理亂，皆將視為適然之故。蠹治害政，可勝言哉！方今
translation_en:
…the sagely and enlightened sovereign: you may indeed be called a loyal and reverent scholar. How could it be merely your writing that deserves selection!

Comment by Examiner Wang, an Instructor: 〔You press those several thinkers with searching questions, leaving them no room for argument. A disciple of Zhongni and a minister upholding the August Norm—surely you are such a man?〕

Comment by Examiner Xu, a Professor: 〔He comprehends the principles of Heaven and humanity. Select him.〕

For a ruler governing all under Heaven, nothing takes precedence over discerning the principles of Heaven and humanity and recognizing the subtle beginnings of their mutual response and communication. Something suddenly occurs, and no one knows its source; whether things converge or diverge, their true circumstances ultimately cannot be concealed. This is what is meant by “subtle beginnings.” Heaven and humanity differ in form and are far apart in their positions. Outwardly they seem separated and opposed, yet in their generation and transformation, waning and waxing, they communicate unseen and operate silently, without the slightest gap. This is the unity of their principle. Once one understands that their principle is one, the means of discerning their subtle beginnings will be found without going beyond it.

Alas, since Zhongni died, the Great Way has ceased to be clear throughout the world. Thus the various thinkers, each following his own understanding, have invoked antiquity to attack the present and given free rein to their tongues, claiming that their understanding of the relation between Heaven and humanity is exceedingly precise. Yet those versed in being [?] fail to understand the unity of its principle, while those immersed in nonbeing fail to discern the wondrous working of its incipient movements. For the most part, they dazzle people with techniques and flaunt their calculations, mixing these with strange and fantastic claims about tokens of Heaven’s mandate, prophecies, and apocryphal writings. When their claims happen to coincide with events and their conjectures hit the mark, they can indeed seem credible and astonishing. But when one subsequently seeks the reasons and cannot find them, all the great anomalies and extraordinary portents under Heaven that bear upon order and disorder will come to be regarded as mere chance occurrences. Can the damage this does to governance and administration ever be fully expressed? At present …

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
是天地之不及者賴聖人而成故曰裁成
天地之道輔相天地之宜以左右民聖人
雖聰明睿知而其見諸禮樂刑政以開先
天下者不能不賴之天天亦未始忘情也
故曰天垂象見吉凶聖人象之河出圖洛
出書聖人則之又曰天乃錫禹洪範九疇
彝倫攸叙如是則人君之與天不啻子之
於父母而呼吸動靜與世相感其理有不
一而其幾有不孚者邪世之君臣往往疑
===
於異同離合之間又見彼數子者議論紛
繆以為彼皆習於春秋洪範者如此將遂
棄其說而不之信呼惑亦甚矣夫孔子修
春秋正王法明天道經世之要先王之志
也故日食星隕山崩地震螽螟水旱書其
事而不著其應說者謂天道遠人道邇聖
人蓋慎之誠是也今考其書比類屬詞因
時覈實雖不明言徵應而所以召致之由
已暴白而不可掩蓋即洪範之精義也箕
punctuated: 是天地之不及者，賴聖人而成。故曰：「裁成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。」聖人雖聰明睿知，而其見諸禮樂刑政，以開先天下者，不能不賴之天。天亦未始忘情也。故曰：「天垂象，見吉凶，聖人象之；河出圖，洛出書，聖人則之。」又曰：「天乃錫禹洪範九疇，彝倫攸叙。」如是，則人君之與天，不啻子之於父母，而呼吸動靜，與世相感，其理有不一，而其幾有不孚者邪？世之君臣往往疑於異同離合之間，又見彼數子者議論紛繆，以為彼皆習於《春秋》《洪範》者如此，將遂棄其說而不之信呼？惑亦甚矣！夫孔子修《春秋》，正王法，明天道，經世之要，先王之志也。故日食、星隕、山崩、地震、螽螟、水旱，書其事而不著其應。說者謂：「天道遠，人道邇，聖人蓋慎之。」誠是也。今考其書，比類屬詞，因時覈實，雖不明言徵應，而所以召致之由，已暴白而不可掩，蓋即《洪範》之精義也。箕
translation_en:
…Thus, what Heaven and Earth leave incomplete depends upon the sage for its completion. Hence it is said: “He shapes and completes the Way of Heaven and Earth, assists what is fitting in Heaven and Earth, and thereby guides the people.” Although the sage possesses keen perception and profound understanding, what he manifests in rites, music, punishments, and government to lead the world forward cannot but depend upon Heaven. Nor has Heaven ever been indifferent. Hence it is said: “Heaven displays images, revealing good and ill fortune, and the sage takes them as his model. The Yellow River brings forth the Chart, and the Luo River brings forth the Writing, and the sage takes them as his rule.” It is also said: “Heaven then bestowed upon Yu the nine divisions of the Great Plan, through which the constant principles of human relations were set in order.”

Thus, the ruler’s relationship to Heaven is nothing less than that of a child to its parents. In breathing, movement, and stillness, he responds reciprocally with the world [?]. Could their underlying principle fail to be one, or their incipient workings fail to correspond? Rulers and ministers often harbor doubts amid differences and similarities, separations and conjunctions. Seeing, moreover, the tangled and contradictory arguments of those several thinkers, they suppose that, since even men versed in the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Great Plan are like this, they should simply discard their teachings and cease to believe them. How profound their confusion is!

Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals to rectify royal standards and clarify the Way of Heaven: these are the essentials of ordering the world and the intentions of the former kings. Thus, concerning solar eclipses, falling stars, collapsing mountains, earthquakes, locusts, grain pests, floods, and droughts, he recorded the events without explicitly identifying what they corresponded to. Commentators say: “The Way of Heaven is distant; the human way is near. The sage was therefore cautious about this.” This is indeed correct. Yet if we now examine his book, compare similar cases, connect its wording, and investigate the facts in their historical circumstances, then, although it does not explicitly state the correspondences of portents, the causes that called them forth are already plainly exposed and cannot be concealed. This is precisely the essential meaning of the Great Plan. Ji…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
子為周武王陳禹所有洪範之書條其事
為九類別其說為九章以天之五行配人
之五事而附庶徵於其間蓋曰五事得則
休徵各以類應五事失則咎徵各以類應
此理之大較也然實重於皇極而庶徵乃
其一疇故必敬以五事厚以八政協以五
紀乂以三德明以稽疑然後本之五行以
驗庶徵之實未嘗分屬類配次其徵應此
即春秋比事不辯之旨大同而小異者也
===
將使人君因其感通之理求體天心畏敬
從事而不敢忽此固箕子深知天理而達
神禹之心也夫洪範之庶徵配以五行五
事他疇固各自為言不相附屬而劉向伏
勝之徒作五行傳强援皇極以足咎徵之
說一虫一木賁以禍福推類相附遂使洪
範之道失其倫理雜沓宂細而與蠢彩角
其得失蓋以人事相與之迹而語天道感
化之妙此愚之所謂不識其理者夾漈鄭
punctuated:
子為周武王陳禹所有《洪範》之書，條其事為九類，別其說為九章，以天之五行配人之五事，而附庶徵於其間。蓋曰：五事得，則休徵各以類應；五事失，則咎徵各以類應。此理之大較也。然實重於皇極，而庶徵乃其一疇，故必敬以五事，厚以八政，協以五紀，乂以三德，明以稽疑，然後本之五行，以驗庶徵之實，未嘗分屬類配，次其徵應。此即《春秋》比事不辯之旨，大同而小異者也。將使人君因其感通之理，求體天心，畏敬從事而不敢忽。此固箕子深知天理而達神禹之心也。
夫《洪範》之庶徵，配以五行、五事，他疇固各自為言，不相附屬。而劉向、伏勝之徒作《五行傳》，强援皇極以足咎徵之說，一虫一木，賁以禍福，推類相附，遂使《洪範》之道失其倫理，雜沓宂細，而與蠢彩角其得失。蓋以人事相與之迹，而語天道感化之妙，此愚之所謂不識其理者。夾漈鄭
translation_en:
…Jizi presented to King Wu of Zhou the text of the Great Plan (Hongfan) that Yu had possessed, arranging its subjects into nine categories and distinguishing its teachings in nine sections. He paired Heaven’s Five Phases with the Five Personal Activities of human beings, incorporating the Various Signs among them. The general point was this: when the Five Activities are properly conducted, favorable signs respond, each according to its kind; when the Five Activities go awry, adverse signs respond, each according to its kind. Such is the broad outline of this principle. Yet the true emphasis lies upon the Sovereign’s Ultimate Standard, while the Various Signs constitute only one of the categories. Thus one must exercise reverence through the Five Activities, enrich the people through the Eight Affairs of Government, establish concord through the Five Measures of Time, govern through the Three Virtues, and attain clarity through the Examination of Doubts. Only then, taking the Five Phases as the foundation, can one verify the realities of the Various Signs. The text never parcels these out into fixed affiliations and matching categories to arrange their signs and responses in sequence. This is substantially the same as the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in juxtaposing events without explicit argument, differing only in minor respects. Its purpose is to lead rulers, through the principle of reciprocal influence and communication, to seek to embody Heaven’s heart and to conduct affairs with awe and reverence, never daring to be negligent. This indeed shows that Jizi deeply understood Heaven’s principles and comprehended the heart of the divinely sagacious Yu.
Now, the Various Signs of the Great Plan are paired with the Five Phases and the Five Activities; the other categories each have their own teachings and are not subordinated to one another. Yet Liu Xiang, Fu Sheng, and their like composed commentaries on the Five Phases, forcibly drawing in the Sovereign’s Ultimate Standard to round out their account of adverse signs. They embellished every insect and every tree with implications of misfortune or good fortune, drawing analogies and attaching things to one another. Consequently, they caused the Way of the Great Plan to lose its coherent order, becoming confused, prolix, and petty, and to compete with “chun cai” [蠢彩, text doubtful] over which predictions proved right or wrong. They used the observable traces of interactions in human affairs to discuss the subtle workings of responsive transformation in Heaven’s Way. This is what I, in my humble opinion, call a failure to understand its principle. Zheng of Jiaji…

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
氏因向勝之失而併疑春秋之傳以為妄
學欺人妖學欺天歐陽修則又稍倣春秋
削五行之徵應存其災異似皆有見矣然
至欲盡去三家褒貶之例五行相應之詞
不免於矯枉過直此則愚之所謂不識其
幾者揆諸闡天弘法之義舉無發明又烏
足以語聖人之道哉書稱天聰明自我民
聰明天明畏自我民明威達於上下敬哉
有土言天人之理一也常厥德保厥位惟
===
吉凶不僭在人惟天降災祥在德言感應
之幾存乎已也故洪水大旱堯湯致治桑
穀雊雉丁戊興王朱鳳芝草無救桓靈之
亂宣公大有年君子猶以為異可以識天
人之際矣然則
今日之
上下交修反異致和參天地而贊化育又豈外
是哉夫災變之來仲舒以為天心仁愛蓋
其震蕩駭異之形皆吾修身圖治之資又
punctuated:
氏因向勝之失，而併疑春秋之傳，以為妄學欺人，妖學欺天。歐陽修則又稍倣春秋，削五行之徵應，存其災異，似皆有見矣。然至欲盡去三家褒貶之例、五行相應之詞，不免於矯枉過直。此則愚之所謂不識其幾者。揆諸闡天弘法之義，舉無發明，又烏足以語聖人之道哉？《書》稱：「天聰明，自我民聰明；天明畏，自我民明威。達於上下，敬哉有土！」言天人之理一也。「常厥德，保厥位，惟吉凶不僭。」「在人惟天，降災祥在德。」言感應之幾存乎已也。故洪水大旱，堯湯致治；桑穀雊雉，丁戊興王；朱鳳芝草，無救桓靈之亂；宣公大有年，君子猶以為異。可以識天人之際矣。
然則今日之上下交修，反異致和，參天地而贊化育，又豈外是哉？夫災變之來，仲舒以為天心仁愛，蓋其震蕩駭異之形，皆吾修身圖治之資，又
translation_en:
…Master Zheng, because of the errors of Liu Xiang and Fu Sheng, went so far as to doubt the commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals as well, regarding them as false learning that deceived people and portent lore that deceived Heaven. Ouyang Xiu, in turn, followed the Spring and Autumn Annals to some extent, deleting accounts of predictive correspondences associated with the Five Phases while retaining records of disasters and anomalies. Both seem to have had some insight. Yet to wish to eliminate entirely the precedents for praise and blame in the three commentarial traditions, along with statements about correspondences among the Five Phases, is inevitably to overcorrect. This is what I mean by failing to understand the subtle beginnings of events. Judged by the purpose of elucidating Heaven and extending its models, neither offers any clarification. How, then, could they adequately discuss the Way of the sages?
The Book of Documents states: “Heaven’s hearing and sight derive from the hearing and sight of our people; Heaven’s manifest awesomeness derives from the manifest authority of our people. This reaches above and below. Be reverent, you who possess territory!” This means that Heaven and humanity share a single principle. “Maintain constancy in your virtue and preserve your position; good and ill fortune never err.” “What rests with human beings rests with Heaven; the sending down of calamities and blessings depends on virtue.” These words mean that the subtle beginnings of stimulus and response lie within oneself. Thus, amid the great flood and severe drought, Yao and Tang achieved good government; amid the portents of mulberry and paper-mulberry trees and a crowing pheasant, Ding and Wu [probably Wuding and Taiwu; ?] brought royal rule to renewed flourishing. Red phoenixes and auspicious fungi could not remedy the disorder under Emperors Huan and Ling. When Duke Xuan enjoyed a year of abundant harvests, the gentleman still regarded it as an anomaly. From these examples one can understand the relationship between Heaven and humanity.
Then, today, when those above and below cultivate themselves together, turn anomalies back into harmony, and stand alongside Heaven and Earth in assisting their transforming and nourishing work, how could this lie outside that same principle? As for the arrival of disasters and abnormal events, Dong Zhongshu regarded them as expressions of Heaven’s benevolent concern. Their unsettling and alarming manifestations are all resources for our cultivation of ourselves and our pursuit of good government; moreover, …

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
何慮焉今欲求其感召之故必將責其嚮
應之實是又所謂其得則某效某失則某
應之謬矣執事所欲聞者豈其然乎愚聞
陰陽不調三辰失行不足懼而賢人隱匿
四民遷業深可畏山崩川涸蝱賊傷稼不
足懼而廉耻道消直言蔑聞深可畏小人
訛謠不足懼而毀譽亂真深可畏今日之
不足懼者未必如彼之甚而其深可畏者
容或有一于是乎誠有之則其所以消弭
===
之者可以深長思矣草茅之士罔知忌諱
執事倘與其進尚當發春秋之旨明皇極
之道以攄芹曝若夫補偏救弊僕僕于事
爲之末蓋將有言焉而未暇也謹對
punctuated: 何慮焉？今欲求其感召之故，必將責其嚮應之實，是又所謂其得則某效、某失則某應之謬矣。執事所欲聞者，豈其然乎？愚聞陰陽不調、三辰失行不足懼，而賢人隱匿、四民遷業深可畏；山崩川涸、蝱賊傷稼不足懼，而廉耻道消、直言蔑聞深可畏；小人訛謠不足懼，而毀譽亂真深可畏。今日之不足懼者，未必如彼之甚，而其深可畏者，容或有一于是乎？誠有之，則其所以消弭之者，可以深長思矣。草茅之士，罔知忌諱。執事倘與其進，尚當發《春秋》之旨，明皇極之道，以攄芹曝。若夫補偏救弊，僕僕于事爲之末，蓋將有言焉，而未暇也。謹對。
translation_en:
…what, then, is there to worry about? If we now seek the reasons why such phenomena are called forth, insisting on concrete evidence of their corresponding responses, we fall once again into the error of claiming that a particular success produces a particular effect, and a particular failure a particular response. Could this really be what you, honored examiners, wish to hear? I have heard that disharmony between yin and yang and deviations in the courses of the three celestial luminaries—the sun, moon, and stars—are not grounds for fear; but worthy men withdrawing into obscurity and the four occupations abandoning their livelihoods are deeply alarming. Mountains collapsing, rivers drying up, and insect pests [?] damaging crops are not grounds for fear; but the decline of integrity and a sense of shame, and the near absence of forthright speech, are deeply alarming. False rumors spread by petty men are not grounds for fear; but praise and blame confounding the truth are deeply alarming. Today, the things that need not be feared may not be as severe as those just described; yet might even one of these deeply alarming conditions exist among us? If so, the means of eliminating it deserve profound and sustained reflection.

As a scholar of humble station, I know nothing of what must be left unsaid. If you, honored examiners, should approve my advancement, I ought further to expound the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals and clarify the Way of the August Ultimate (huangji), thereby offering my humble counsel—as one who offers celery or the warmth of the sun. As for correcting imbalances and remedying abuses through tireless attention to the details of practical affairs, I would have more to say, but time does not permit. Respectfully submitted.

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄後序
是歲八月既望河南鄉試事
竣錄且告成矣〔應 槐〕以執事
當序諸末簡乃言曰錄也者
錄多士之名與文以示不朽
者也夫以一日之文見錄於
有司而遂謂名與文皆於是
===
乎在此衆人之見而君子之
所深懼也是故虛車而飾用
者勿取過情之譽君子耻之
可弗懼乎我
國家設科取士豈惟詞華之尚
而聲稱之貴將以責其行考
其實以求真才焉耳然文者
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄後序

是歲八月既望，河南鄉試事竣，錄且告成矣。〔應 槐〕以執事，當序諸末簡，乃言曰：「錄也者，錄多士之名與文以示不朽者也。夫以一日之文見錄於有司，而遂謂名與文皆於是乎在，此衆人之見，而君子之所深懼也。是故虛車而飾用者勿取，過情之譽，君子耻之，可弗懼乎？我國家設科取士，豈惟詞華之尚，而聲稱之貴？將以責其行，考其實，以求真才焉耳。然文者
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

On the day after the full moon in the eighth month of this year, the business of the Henan Provincial Examination was concluded, and its record was also nearing completion. As one of the officials conducting the examination, Ying Huai 〔應 槐〕 was charged with composing a postface for its concluding pages. He therefore writes:

“A record records the names and writings of the many candidates so that they may endure. Yet to have a single day’s writing selected by the responsible officials, and thereupon to suppose that both one’s name and one’s writing are thus secured—this is the view of ordinary people, but something a gentleman deeply fears. Thus, an empty carriage ornamented for use is not to be chosen [?]; praise exceeding the reality is something a gentleman considers shameful. Can one fail to be apprehensive?

“Our dynasty established examinations to select men for service. Could its purpose be merely to esteem literary brilliance and prize reputation? It intends to hold them accountable for their conduct and examine their actual accomplishments, thereby seeking genuine talent. Yet as for writing …

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
text:
公私之念決是非之見定而
好惡之情公義利之辨明而
取舍之分嚴此固多士之文
用以應世者果無悖焉則行
成而實著文可以華國而名
可以永世矣夫是之謂不朽
爾諸士盍亦知所圖哉〔應 槐〕
===
責在校文而多士以文進故
於終也舉是為之告多士其
勗諸〔應 槐〕亦將籍以無懼矣
山東東昌府高唐州儒學學
正王〔應 槐〕謹序
punctuated:
公私之念決，是非之見定，而好惡之情公；義利之辨明，而取舍之分嚴。此固多士之文，用以應世者果無悖焉，則行成而實著，文可以華國，而名可以永世矣。夫是之謂不朽，爾諸士盍亦知所圖哉？〔應 槐〕責在校文，而多士以文進，故於終也，舉是為之告。多士其勗諸！〔應 槐〕亦將籍以無懼矣。
山東東昌府高唐州儒學學正王〔應 槐〕謹序。
translation_en:
…when thoughts of public interest and private advantage are clearly distinguished, judgments of right and wrong are settled, and feelings of liking and disliking are impartial; when the distinction between righteousness and profit is clear, and the discrimination between what to accept and what to reject is strict. These are surely qualities of the candidates’ writing. If what they put into practice in their dealings with the world truly accords with these principles, their conduct will become accomplished and their substantive worth manifest. Their writing can then bring lustre to the state, and their names endure through the ages. This is what is called immortality. Should you candidates not also understand what you ought to strive for?
I, Yinghuai, am responsible for evaluating writing, while the candidates seek advancement through writing. Thus, at the close, I set forth these matters to admonish them. May all the candidates exert themselves! I, Yinghuai, shall thereby also have grounds to be free of apprehension.
Preface respectfully composed by Wang Yinghuai, Director of the Confucian School of Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong.

title: 嘉靖十三年河南鄉試錄
